Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line puzzle asks: "I am an integer. My distance from zero is 7, but I am LESS than zero." What integer am I?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: −7 — it has a distance of 7 from zero (matching the clue) and is less than zero (negative), matching both given conditions.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line puzzle asks: "I am an integer. I am the opposite of an opposite of −15." What integer am I?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: −15 — taking the opposite of the opposite of any integer always returns the original integer itself.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A weather satellite tracks temperature changes along a vertical number-line-style scale from the ground (0°C reference) up through the atmosphere, where temperature generally DECREASES with altitude (unlike a typical number line where higher position means a higher value). Why might this scenario require EXTRA care when interpreting integer positions compared to a standard horizontal number line?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: Since temperature here decreases as altitude (position) increases, the usual number-line rule of "further right/higher position equals greater value" does NOT directly apply to the temperature values themselves, even though it still applies to the ALTITUDE positions — this requires carefully distinguishing between the position scale (altitude) and the value being measured (temperature), which behave inversely in this specific scenario.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line based "integer duel" game has two players choose integers, and whoever picks the integer FARTHER from zero (regardless of sign) wins that round. Player 1 picks −40, Player 2 picks +25. Who wins this round, and why?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: Player 1 wins, since −40 has a distance of 40 from zero, which is greater than Player 2’s distance of 25 from zero — in THIS specific game, distance from zero (not the integer’s actual greater/lesser value) determines the winner.

Integers on the Number Line.q: Why is it important to clearly distinguish between "which integer is GREATER" (using standard number-line ordering) versus "which integer has the GREATER DISTANCE from zero" (ignoring sign), as these can give completely different answers?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: These two comparisons answer fundamentally different questions: "greater" considers the actual signed value and direction (where positive always beats negative), while "distance from zero" only considers magnitude regardless of direction — mixing up these two ideas can lead to incorrect conclusions, such as thinking −40 is "more" than +25 in standard value comparison, when actually +25 is the greater INTEGER (even though −40 has greater distance from zero).

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line based elevator system in a very tall building has floors from −5 (deep basement levels) to +60 (high upper floors), with 0 as the ground floor lobby. A maintenance worker needs to travel from floor −3 to floor +2. How many total floors must the elevator travel through?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: 5 floors total — moving from −3 up to 0 covers 3 floors, then from 0 up to +2 covers 2 more floors, totaling 3+2=5 floors of travel.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line shows a "tied" scenario where two different real-world quantities both correspond to the integer −8 (e.g., a temperature of −8°C and a financial loss of ₹8 represented as −8). Even though both are represented by the same integer, why are they fundamentally different in real-world meaning?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: Even though both situations share the same NUMERICAL integer value (−8) on their respective number-line representations, they describe entirely different physical or real-world quantities (temperature vs money) with different units and contexts — the integer itself is just an abstract mathematical representation, and its real-world meaning depends entirely on what that particular number line is being used to measure.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A space mission tracks a rocket’s altitude on a number line, with Earth’s surface as 0, increasing positively as the rocket ascends. At a certain point, mission control records the rocket’s position as exactly 0 again, AFTER it had already reached positive altitudes earlier in the mission. What does this likely indicate about the rocket’s journey?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: It likely indicates that the rocket has returned to (or near) Earth’s surface again, after having previously ascended to positive altitudes — essentially, this could represent a launch, ascent, and then a return/landing sequence.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line representing a video game character’s "score streak" ranges from −20 (worst possible streak of failures) to +20 (best possible streak of successes), with 0 as a neutral starting point. If a player’s current position is −15, and a single new failure moves them 1 step further left (more negative), what would their NEW position be, and what does this suggest about how close they are to the absolute worst possible streak?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: Their new position would be −16, and since the worst possible streak is −20, they would then be only 4 steps away from reaching that absolute worst position on the number line.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line "tug of war" between two debate teams tracks audience opinion shifts, where 0 represents a perfectly neutral audience, positive integers favor Team A, and negative integers favor Team B. If the position shifts from +5 to −5 over the course of a debate, what does this specifically indicate about how audience opinion changed?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: It indicates that audience opinion shifted from moderately favoring Team A (+5) all the way to equally favoring Team B (−5) by the same magnitude, representing a complete reversal in audience sentiment from one side to the other.

Integers on the Number Line.q: Why might mathematicians describe the number line as being "symmetric" around zero, and how does this relate directly to the concept of opposite integers?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: The number line is symmetric around zero because for every point at a certain distance to the right of zero (a positive integer), there is a matching point at the exact same distance to the left of zero (its negative opposite) — this mirror-like balance around the zero point is precisely what defines and visually represents the concept of opposite integers.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line based "risk meter" for a financial investment ranges from −100 (total loss) to +100 (maximum possible gain), with 0 representing breaking even. An investment currently shows a reading of −30. Without any further calculation, what TWO pieces of information can you immediately determine just from this single integer reading?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: You can immediately determine: (1) the investment currently represents a LOSS (since the value is negative), and (2) the size of that loss relative to the maximum possible loss is 30 out of a possible 100, giving a sense of how severe the current loss is on this particular risk scale.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A number line shows integer positions for three towns along a straight desert highway: Town X at −80km, Town Y at 0km (the highway’s reference marker), and Town Z at +120km. A traveler starts at Town Y. Which town is FARTHER from the traveler’s starting point, and by how much more?
Integers on the Number Line.answer: Town Z is farther, since its distance from Town Y is 120km, compared to Town X’s distance of 80km — Town Z is 40km farther than Town X from the starting point.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 6 + 4?
Addition of Integers.answer: 10 (both positive, simply add).
−10 (both negative: add the values, keep the negative sign).

Addition of Integers.q: What is 9 + (−2)?
Addition of Integers.answer: 7 (different signs: 9 is bigger, 9−2=7, keep positive sign).

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−9) + 2?
Addition of Integers.answer: −7 (different signs: 9 is bigger and negative, 9−2=7, keep negative sign).

Addition of Integers.q: What is the rule when adding two integers with the SAME sign?
Addition of Integers.answer: Add their values together and keep that same sign for the answer.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the rule when adding two integers with DIFFERENT signs?
Addition of Integers.answer: Subtract the smaller value from the bigger value (ignoring signs), and use the sign of whichever integer was originally bigger.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 0 + 8?
Addition of Integers.answer: 8 (adding zero never changes the other integer).

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−5) + 0?
Addition of Integers.answer: −5 (adding zero never changes the other integer).

Addition of Integers.q: What is 7 + (−7)?
Addition of Integers.answer: 0 (adding an integer and its opposite always gives zero).

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−12) + 12?
Addition of Integers.answer: 0 (opposite integers always add to zero).

Addition of Integers.q: A temperature is 6°C and drops by 10 degrees. Write this as an addition and find the new temperature.
A temperature is −3°C and rises by 8 degrees. Write this as an addition and find the new temperature.
A football team gains 6 yards, then loses 10 yards. Write this as an addition and find the total change.
Addition of Integers.answer: 6 + (−10) = −4 yards (a net loss of 4 yards).

Addition of Integers.q: A submarine at −50m rises by 20m. Write this as an addition and find the new depth.
Explain step by step how to add two integers with the same sign, using 7 and 5 (both negative) as an example.
steps: Recognize both integers, −7 and −5, have the same (negative) sign.
Apply the common negative sign to the result: −12.
Addition of Integers.answer: Add the values (7+5=12) and keep the shared negative sign: (−7)+(−5)=−12.

Addition of Integers.q: Explain step by step how to add two integers with different signs, using 10 and −4 as an example.
steps: Identify that 10 and −4 have different signs.
Find the bigger value ignoring signs: 10 is bigger than 4.
Subtract the smaller from the bigger: 10−4=6.
Since 10 was positive, the answer keeps a positive sign: +6.
Addition of Integers.answer: Subtract 4 from 10 (=6) and keep the positive sign since 10 was the bigger value: 10+(−4)=6.
−35 (both negative: add the values, keep the negative sign).

Addition of Integers.q: What is 18 + (−25)?
Addition of Integers.answer: −7 (different signs: 25 is bigger and negative, 25−18=7, keep negative sign).

Addition of Integers.q: A bank balance is +₹100 and a withdrawal of ₹150 is made. Write this as an addition and find the new balance.
A bank balance is −₹80 and a deposit of ₹80 is made. Write this as an addition and find the new balance.
Addition of Integers.answer: (−80) + 80 = 0 (exactly balanced, neither owing nor having extra).

Addition of Integers.q: What is the additive inverse of 18?
What is the additive inverse of −25?
How do you find the additive inverse of any integer?
Addition of Integers.answer: Simply flip its sign — positive becomes negative, and negative becomes positive (zero stays zero).

Addition of Integers.q: A hiker starts at +500m elevation and descends 700m. Write this as an addition and find the new elevation.
A hiker starts at −300m elevation and climbs 450m. Write this as an addition and find the new elevation.

Addition of Integers.answer: −100 (both negative: add the values, keep the negative sign).

Addition of Integers.q: What is 33 + (−33)?
Addition of Integers.answer: 0 (opposite integers add to zero).

Addition of Integers.q: A company’s profit is recorded as +₹5000 in one month and a loss of ₹8000 the next month. What is the combined result over both months?
Addition of Integers.answer: 5000 + (−8000) = −3000, meaning an overall loss of ₹3000 across both months.

Addition of Integers.q: Why does adding two negative integers always give a MORE negative (smaller) result, never a positive one?
Addition of Integers.answer: Since both integers represent movement in the negative direction (to the left of zero), combining them moves even further left, away from zero in the negative direction, so the result must also be negative.

Addition of Integers.q: Why does adding two positive integers always give a result that is even MORE positive (bigger)?
Addition of Integers.answer: Since both integers represent movement in the positive direction (to the right of zero), combining them moves even further right, so the result must also be positive and larger than either original integer.

Addition of Integers.q: A weather balloon rises 1200m, then later descends 1500m. What is its overall change in height?
Addition of Integers.answer: 1200 + (−1500) = −300m, meaning the balloon ends up 300m lower than where it started.

Addition of Integers.q: A video game character gains +50 points, then loses 50 points. What is their final score change?
Addition of Integers.answer: 50 + (−50) = 0, meaning no overall change in score.

Addition of Integers.q: Explain step by step why the SIGN of the answer when adding two different-signed integers depends on which original number had the BIGGER value (ignoring signs).
steps: Picture the addition as a number-line hop: starting at one integer, then hopping toward (or past) zero based on the second integer’s sign and size.

If the starting integer’s distance from zero is bigger than the hop’s size, you will overshoot zero in the hop’s direction but not reach all the way back past zero, so you land on the SAME side as the bigger original value.
Therefore, the final answer keeps the sign of whichever integer had the larger absolute value, since that integer "wins" the tug-of-war toward its own direction.
Addition of Integers.answer: The larger-magnitude integer "pulls" the result toward its own side of zero, so the final sign matches whichever original integer had the bigger value (ignoring sign).

Addition of Integers.q: A scuba diver is at −18m and swims up 25m. What is their new position?
Addition of Integers.answer: (−18) + 25 = 7m (now above sea level, at +7m).

Addition of Integers.q: A scuba diver is at −18m and swims up only 10m. What is their new position?
Addition of Integers.answer: (−18) + 10 = −8m (still below sea level, but closer to the surface).

Addition of Integers.q: A spreadsheet records daily temperature CHANGES (not actual temperatures) as: +3, −5, +2, −1. What is the TOTAL change over these 4 days?
Addition of Integers.answer: 3+(−5)+2+(−1) = (3+2) + (−5−1) = 5 + (−6) = −1, meaning an overall drop of 1 degree across the 4 days.

Addition of Integers.q: A number line shows a token starting at −4. It then hops +7. Where does it land?
A number line shows a token starting at 9. It then hops −15. Where does it land?
A delivery truck travels +120km (away from the depot), then −45km (back toward the depot). What is its net position relative to the depot?
Addition of Integers.answer: 120 + (−45) = 75km (still 75km away from the depot, in the original direction).

Addition of Integers.q: Why is it impossible for the SAME-SIGN addition rule (just adding values and keeping the sign) to ever produce a result smaller (closer to zero) than either of the two original integers?
Addition of Integers.answer: Because combining two values moving in the same direction always moves FURTHER in that direction, away from zero, never closer to it — the combined distance from zero can only grow, not shrink, when both contributions push the same way.

Addition of Integers.q: A stock price changes by +₹15 on Monday and −₹22 on Tuesday. What is the net 2-day change?
Addition of Integers.answer: 15 + (−22) = −7, meaning an overall drop of ₹7 across the two days.

Addition of Integers.q: A stock price changes by −₹8 on Monday and −₹14 on Tuesday. What is the net 2-day change?
Addition of Integers.answer: (−8) + (−14) = −22, meaning an overall drop of ₹22 across the two days.

Addition of Integers.q: A number line addition problem reads: (−25) + 25 + (−10). Solve this step by step.
Addition of Integers.answer: First, (−25)+25=0 (opposites cancel). Then, 0+(−10)=−10. The final answer is −10.

Addition of Integers.q: A spacecraft’s altitude changes are recorded over 4 stages of a mission as: +8000m, −3000m, +1500m, −500m (relative to the previous stage). What is the TOTAL net change in altitude across all 4 stages combined?
Explain step by step how a financial analyst would calculate a company’s NET profit or loss across 5 quarters, given quarterly results of: +200000, −50000, +75000, −120000, +30000 (in rupees).
steps: Group all the positive values together and add them: 200000+75000+30000 = 305000.
Group all the negative values together and add them: (−50000)+(−120000) = −170000.
Add the two group totals together: 305000 + (−170000) = 135000.
Conclude the company had a net profit of ₹135,000 across all 5 quarters combined.
Addition of Integers.answer: Adding all positives (305000) and all negatives (−170000) together gives a net result of +135000, meaning an overall profit of ₹1,35,000.

Addition of Integers.q: A mountain climbing expedition records elevation CHANGES (not absolute elevations) at each camp transition as: +1200m, +800m, −300m, +1500m, −2700m. Does the expedition end up HIGHER or LOWER than where it started, and by how much?

A video game’s scoring system awards +10 points for a win, −15 points for a loss, and +5 points for a draw. Over 6 games, a player records: win, loss, draw, win, loss, win. Calculate the player’s total score using integer addition.
A scientist tracks a chemical reaction’s temperature changes (in °C) at 5-minute intervals as: +12, −8, +3, −15, +20, −6. What is the cumulative (total) temperature change after all 6 intervals?

Why might breaking a long addition problem with MANY positive and negative integers into "group all positives, group all negatives, then combine" be a more EFFICIENT strategy than adding them strictly in the original left-to-right order?
Addition of Integers.answer: Grouping similar signs together reduces the number of "sign-switching" subtraction-style calculations needed, since you only need ONE final same-sign-vs-different-sign comparison at the very end, rather than repeatedly recalculating signs at every single step along the way — this often makes mental math faster and reduces the chance of sign errors.

Addition of Integers.q: A number line "treasure hunt" game has a player starting at 0, then following clues that say "move +15, then −22, then +8, then −3, then +30." Where does the player END UP, and what is the player’s FINAL distance from the starting point (0)?
Addition of Integers.answer: 0+15+(−22)+8+(−3)+30 = (15+8+30)+(−22−3) = 53+(−25) = 28. The player ends up at position 28, which is also their final distance (28 units) from the starting point.

Addition of Integers.q: A weather model predicts temperature swings over 24 hours in 4-hour blocks as: −2, +5, +9, −4, −7, +3 (in °C, relative to the previous block). If the starting temperature at hour 0 was 18°C, what is the temperature at the END of all 24 hours?

A hot air balloon’s altitude changes during a flight are recorded as: −150m, −80m, +220m, −40m, +95m (positive means rising, negative means descending). If the balloon started at an altitude of 300m, what is its FINAL altitude after all these changes?

A school fundraiser tracks daily donations and expenses as integers over a week: +500, −150, +800, −300, +1200, −450, +200 (in rupees, where positive is donations received and negative is expenses paid). What is the NET financial result for the entire week?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 500+800+1200+200=2700. Sum of negatives: (−150)+(−300)+(−450)=−900. Net total: 2700+(−900)=1800, meaning a net gain of ₹1800 for the week.

Addition of Integers.q: Explain step by step why, when adding a LONG list of integers with mixed signs, the FINAL answer’s sign cannot always be predicted just by looking at how many positive versus negative numbers are in the list (i.e., having MORE negative numbers in the list doesn’t guarantee a negative final answer).
steps: Recognize that the SIGN of the final answer depends on the actual VALUES being added, not just the COUNT of positive versus negative numbers.

Consider an example: three negative integers of small value (−1, −1, −1) versus one positive integer of large value (+10). Even though there are MORE negative numbers (3 vs 1), the positive value’s magnitude can still dominate.
Calculate: (−1)+(−1)+(−1)+10 = (−3)+10 = 7, which is POSITIVE despite having more negative terms in the list.
Conclude that the final sign depends on the total MAGNITUDE of all positives compared to the total magnitude of all negatives, not simply how many of each there are.
Addition of Integers.answer: The final sign depends on comparing the TOTAL magnitude of all positive values against the TOTAL magnitude of all negative values, not on which group has more individual numbers — a few large positives can easily outweigh many small negatives, or vice versa.

Addition of Integers.q: A drone’s battery percentage changes during a flight are recorded as: −5%, −8%, +2% (a brief recharge from solar panels), −12%, −3%. If the drone started with 100% battery, what is its battery percentage at the end of the flight?

A cricket team’s net run rate changes after each match in a tournament are recorded as: +0.8, −1.2, +0.5, +0.3, −0.6 (these are decimals, not integers, but follow the same addition logic). What is the TOTAL net run rate change after all 5 matches?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 0.8+0.5+0.3=1.6. Sum of negatives: (−1.2)+(−0.6)=−1.8. Total: 1.6+(−1.8)=−0.2, meaning an overall slight decrease in net run rate.

Addition of Integers.q: A construction project’s timeline changes (in days, where positive means ahead of schedule and negative means delayed) are tracked weekly as: +2, −5, −3, +6, −1, +4. Is the project, OVERALL, ahead of or behind its original schedule after these 6 weeks, and by how many days?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 2+6+4=12. Sum of negatives: (−5)+(−3)+(−1)=−9. Total: 12+(−9)=3, meaning the project is 3 days AHEAD of its original schedule overall.

Addition of Integers.q: A river’s water level changes (in cm, relative to a marked reference point) are recorded over 5 days of varying rainfall as: +15, +22, −8, +30, −45. Did the river level RISE or FALL overall compared to the reference point, and by how much?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 15+22+30=67. Sum of negatives: (−8)+(−45)=−53. Total: 67+(−53)=14cm, meaning the river level ROSE overall by 14cm compared to the reference point.

Addition of Integers.q: A satellite’s fuel reserve (in kg) changes during various maneuvers are recorded as: −12, −8, −20, +5 (a fuel transfer received), −15. If the satellite started with 200kg of fuel, how much fuel remains after all these maneuvers?

A classroom experiment tracks a toy car’s position changes (in cm, where positive is forward and negative is backward) on a track as: +25, −10, +40, −60, +15, −5. What is the car’s FINAL position relative to its starting point?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 25+40+15=80. Sum of negatives: (−10)+(−60)+(−5)=−75. Total: 80+(−75)=5cm forward from the starting point.

Addition of Integers.q: A weather satellite measures pressure changes (in hPa, a unit of atmospheric pressure) across 6 readings as: +3, +5, −2, +7, −9, −4. What is the TOTAL pressure change across all readings?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 3+5+7=15. Sum of negatives: (−2)+(−9)+(−4)=−15. Total: 15+(−15)=0, meaning NO net change in pressure overall, even though individual readings varied.

Addition of Integers.q: Why might the result from the previous pressure-change question (a total of exactly 0) be a particularly interesting or notable outcome for a scientist analyzing this data?
Addition of Integers.answer: A net change of exactly zero suggests that, despite several individual fluctuations up and down, the overall atmospheric pressure returned to (or remained statistically the same as) its starting level by the end of the measurement period — this could indicate a stable weather pattern or a temporary, self-correcting disturbance.

Addition of Integers.q: A factory’s daily production numbers (relative to a daily target, as integers) over a work week are: +50, −30, +20, −45, +60, −15. Is the factory, OVERALL for the week, ahead of or behind its combined daily targets, and by how much?
Addition of Integers.answer: Sum of positives: 50+20+60=130. Sum of negatives: (−30)+(−45)+(−15)=−90. Total: 130+(−90)=40 units ahead of the combined target overall for the week.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is the general rule for subtracting integers?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: a − b = a + (−b): subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What are the 3 steps for subtracting integers?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Keep the first integer the same, change the subtraction sign to addition, and change the second integer to its opposite.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is 9 − 4?
What is 9 − (−4)?
What is (−9) − 4?
What does "subtracting a negative integer" become, in terms of addition?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: It becomes adding a positive integer, since the opposite of a negative is positive.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is 7 − 7?

Subtraction of Integers.answer: 0 (any integer minus itself equals zero, even for negatives).

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is 0 − 6?
What is 0 − (−6)?
A temperature is 8°C and drops to a level 12 less. Write this as a subtraction and solve.
A submarine is at −15m. Find how much shallower a point at −5m is, using subtraction.
Explain step by step how to solve (−6) − (−10) using the 3-step subtraction method.
steps: Keep the first integer the same: −6.
Change the subtraction sign to addition: −6 +.
Change the second integer, −10, to its opposite, +10: −6 + 10.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is 14 − 20?
What is 14 − (−20)?
What is (−14) − 20?
Why is it helpful to convert EVERY subtraction problem into an addition problem before solving?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Because it lets you use the same, already-learned addition rules (same-sign and different-sign rules) for every problem, instead of needing a separate, more confusing set of rules just for subtraction.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A hiker is at +300m. Find how much higher this is than a hiker at −100m, using subtraction.
What is 25 − 30?
What is 25 − (−30)?
What is (−25) − 30?
A bank balance is ₹40. A fee of ₹65 is subtracted. What is the new balance?
A bank balance is −₹40 (overdrawn). A correction subtracts a PREVIOUS overdraft fee of −₹65 (meaning the fee is reversed/removed). What is the new balance? (i.e., calculate (−40) − (−65))
Subtraction of Integers.answer: (−40) − (−65) = (−40) + 65 = 25 (now in credit by ₹25, since the fee was removed).

Subtraction of Integers.q: Why does "subtracting a negative" feel confusing at first, even though the rule is simple?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Because in everyday language, subtraction usually means "taking away" or making something smaller, but subtracting a negative actually makes the result BIGGER, which feels opposite to our usual intuition about subtraction.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A weather record shows today’s low was −3°C and yesterday’s low was −11°C. How much warmer was today’s low than yesterday’s? (Calculate today minus yesterday.)
A plane is flying at +9000m altitude. A submarine is at −200m. What is the DIFFERENCE in their positions (plane’s altitude minus submarine’s position)?
Explain step by step why a − (−b) always simplifies to a + b, using the formal subtraction rule.
steps: Start with the general subtraction rule: a − b = a + (−b).
Substitute −b in place of b, since we are subtracting a negative integer this time: a − (−b) = a + (−(−b)).
Recognize that the opposite of a negative number, −(−b), is simply the positive version, b.
Substitute this back in: a − (−b) = a + b.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Using the subtraction rule and recognizing that the opposite of −b is b, a − (−b) simplifies to a + b.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A hot air balloon is at −20m relative to a hilltop launch point (meaning it has descended below the launch point). A nearby drone is at +35m relative to the same point. What is the difference between the drone’s and balloon’s positions?
A scientist needs to find the difference between a reading of −18 units and a reading of −45 units (first minus second). Solve: (−18) − (−45).
Why is "the difference between two integers" often calculated using subtraction in a specific order (first minus second), and what happens if you reverse the order?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Subtracting in a specific order (first minus second) tells you not just the SIZE of the difference but also its DIRECTION (which one is bigger); reversing the order simply flips the sign of the result (e.g., 8−3=5, but 3−8=−5), so order matters when direction/sign is meaningful.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is (−7) − (−7) − (−7)? (Solve step by step, left to right.)
What is 20 − 5 − (−5)? (Solve step by step, left to right.)
A number line shows points at −8 and +12. Find the distance between them using subtraction (larger minus smaller).
A number line shows points at −30 and −5. Find the distance between them using subtraction (larger minus smaller).
Why does finding "distance between two points" on a number line ALWAYS give a positive result, even though subtraction can sometimes give negative answers?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: As long as you subtract the SMALLER integer from the LARGER one (in the correct order), the result will always be positive, since you are measuring how much farther one point is than the other — doing it in the wrong order would give a negative number representing the same distance but with a direction indicator.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A weather station compares the record HIGH temperature of +42°C with the record LOW temperature of −18°C for a particular city. What is the total TEMPERATURE RANGE (difference between the highest and lowest recorded temperatures)?
A geologist compares the elevation of a mountain peak at +6200m with the elevation of a nearby ocean trench at −9800m. What is the total VERTICAL DISTANCE between these two points?
Explain step by step how the subtraction rule (a − b = a + (−b)) can be used to PROVE that subtracting a negative number always increases the value, regardless of the specific numbers involved.
steps: Start with any subtraction of a negative integer: a − (−b), where b is a positive number.
Apply the subtraction rule: a − (−b) = a + (−(−b)).
Simplify −(−b) to b (the opposite of a negative is positive).
This gives a + b, which is ALWAYS greater than the original value a alone, since you are adding a positive amount b to it — proving the result always increases.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Since a − (−b) always simplifies to a + b, and adding any positive number b always increases the original value a, subtracting a negative number always increases the result.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A financial analyst compares Company A’s profit of +₹500000 with Company B’s loss of −₹200000 for the same quarter. What is the DIFFERENCE in their financial performance (Company A minus Company B)?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: 500000 − (−200000) = 500000 + 200000 = 700000, meaning Company A performed ₹7,00,000 better than Company B that quarter.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A spacecraft’s mission log shows its altitude at Stage 1 as −50m (below the launch platform, in an underground silo) and at Stage 2 as +12000m (in orbit). What is the total change in altitude between these two stages?

A sports analytics team compares a basketball player’s best single-game score differential (team points minus opponent points) of +35 with their worst differential of −28 across a season. What is the TOTAL RANGE between their best and worst performances?

Why might understanding the subtraction-as-addition-of-opposite rule be ESPECIALLY important when working with very large real-world negative numbers, such as national debt figures or extreme temperature records, where mental shortcuts without the rule could easily lead to sign errors?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: With very large numbers, manually tracking multiple sign flips without a clear, systematic rule increases the risk of errors; the formal rule (a−b=a+(−b)) provides a reliable, step-by-step method that removes guesswork and reduces the chance of a costly sign mistake in important real-world calculations.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A chemistry experiment records a reaction’s temperature change starting at −5°C and ending at +95°C. Using subtraction, what is the total temperature INCREASE during the experiment?
A city’s lowest recorded elevation point is −15m (below sea level) and its highest point is +850m. What is the city’s total ELEVATION RANGE?

A number line based "tug of war" game ends with Team A’s final position at +22 and Team B’s starting reference at −22 (their respective extreme ends). Using subtraction, find the TOTAL LENGTH of the playing field represented by these two extreme positions.

Explain step by step why, when calculating the DIFFERENCE between two negative numbers like −5 and −20, many students mistakenly think the answer should also be a "small" negative number, when it actually is NOT.
steps: Students often see two negative numbers and assume subtracting them will simply produce another negative or very small result, due to surface-level pattern matching with the negative signs.
However, applying the formal rule, (−5) − (−20) = (−5) + 20 = 15, shows the actual result is a clearly POSITIVE number.
This happens because subtracting a MORE negative number (−20, which is smaller in value than −5) is mathematically similar to adding a relatively large positive value to −5.
The key insight is that −20 is actually SMALLER (more negative) than −5, so subtracting it (removing an even smaller/more negative amount) results in a NET INCREASE rather than a decrease.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Since −20 is more negative (smaller) than −5, subtracting it removes a smaller, more negative amount, resulting in a clear positive increase (15), not a small negative number as some students might mistakenly assume.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A research vessel measures ocean depth at two locations as integers: −2500m and −7800m. Using subtraction, find how much DEEPER the second location is compared to the first.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: (−7800) − (−2500) = (−7800) + 2500 = −5300. Ignoring the sign (since we want a depth difference, not a position), the second location is 5300m deeper than the first.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A satellite tracks a debris field’s position changes over time: starting position −1200km (relative to a reference orbit), ending position +800km. What is the TOTAL distance the debris field has shifted?

A historian calculates the time span between an event in 450 BCE (treated as approximately −450 for calculation purposes) and an event in 320 CE (treated as +320). Using subtraction, estimate the total number of years between these events.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: 320 − (−450) = 320 + 450 = 770 years between the events (this is an approximation due to historical calendar conventions, but illustrates the integer subtraction concept).

Subtraction of Integers.q: A stock’s value changed from −₹15 (relative to its issue price, meaning it traded ₹15 below issue price) to +₹40 (₹40 above issue price) over one year. What was the total INCREASE in the stock’s relative value over the year?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: 40 − (−15) = 40 + 15 = 55, meaning the stock’s relative value increased by ₹55 over the year.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A robotics competition scores teams using integers, where a team’s WORST round score was −30 and BEST round score was +85. What is the TOTAL RANGE between their best and worst rounds?
A weather balloon’s recorded pressure (in a specialized unit, relative to a baseline) changes from −60 units at launch to +25 units at peak altitude. What is the TOTAL pressure change?

Why might engineers specifically prefer using the subtraction-as-addition-of-opposite method (rather than trying to memorize many separate subtraction rules for different sign combinations) when programming calculations into automated systems or software?
Subtraction of Integers.answer: Using one single, consistent rule (converting subtraction into addition of the opposite) simplifies the logic needed in code, reducing the number of separate conditional cases the software needs to check, which makes the system more reliable, easier to test, and less prone to bugs from missed edge cases.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A number line puzzle states: "The difference between two integers is 18. One of the integers is −7. What could the other integer be?" Find ONE possible answer.
Subtraction of Integers.answer: One possible answer: 11, since 11 − (−7) = 11 + 7 = 18. (Another valid answer: −25, since (−7) − (−25) = (−7) + 25 = 18.)

Subtraction of Integers.q: A scientist studying two chemical samples finds Sample X has a pH-related integer value of −4 and Sample Y has a value of +9. What is the integer DIFFERENCE between Sample Y and Sample X?

Ordering Integers.q: What does the symbol > mean?
Ordering Integers.answer: "Greater than" — the value on the left is bigger than the value on the right.

Ordering Integers.q: What does the symbol < mean?
Ordering Integers.answer: "Less than" — the value on the left is smaller than the value on the right.

Ordering Integers.q: On a number line, which direction means "greater"?
Ordering Integers.answer: To the right — an integer further right is always greater.

Ordering Integers.q: Is 7 greater than or less than 2?
Ordering Integers.answer: 7 is greater than 2 (7 > 2).

Ordering Integers.q: Is −7 greater than or less than −2?
Ordering Integers.answer: −7 is less than −2 (−7 < −2), since −7 is further left.

Ordering Integers.q: Is every positive integer greater than every negative integer?
Ordering Integers.answer: Yes — this is always true, regardless of the specific values involved.

Ordering Integers.q: Among −3, −10, −1, which is the smallest?
Ordering Integers.answer: −10, since it is furthest left (most negative).

Ordering Integers.q: Among −3, −10, −1, which is the largest?
Ordering Integers.answer: −1, since it is closest to zero (furthest right among these three).

Ordering Integers.q: What is "ascending order"?
Ordering Integers.answer: Arranging numbers from smallest to largest.

Ordering Integers.q: What is "descending order"?
Ordering Integers.answer: Arranging numbers from largest to smallest.

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange 4, −2, 0, −9 in ascending order.
Arrange 4, −2, 0, −9 in descending order.
Fill in the correct symbol: −5 ___ 3
Ordering Integers.answer: < (−5 < 3, since −5 is to the left of 3).

Ordering Integers.q: Fill in the correct symbol: 8 ___ −1
Ordering Integers.answer: > (8 > −1, since 8 is to the right of −1).

Ordering Integers.q: Why is it a common mistake to think −10 is "bigger" than −2, just because 10 is bigger than 2?
Ordering Integers.answer: Because when comparing actual integer VALUES (with sign), −10 is further left on the number line and therefore SMALLER than −2, even though the digit 10 looks bigger than 2 if you ignore the negative sign.

Ordering Integers.q: Explain step by step how to arrange a mixed list of positive and negative integers in ascending order.
steps: Separate the integers into negative, zero, and positive groups (if helpful).
Order the negative integers from most negative (smallest) to least negative (closest to zero).
Place zero (if present) after the negatives and before the positives.
Order the positive integers from smallest to largest, placing them after zero.
Ordering Integers.answer: Order negatives from most negative to least negative, then zero, then positives from smallest to largest, to get the full ascending order.

Ordering Integers.q: Two temperatures are −9°C and −2°C. Which is warmer?
Ordering Integers.answer: −2°C is warmer, since −2 is greater than −9 (closer to zero).

Ordering Integers.q: Two submarine depths are −300m and −150m. Which is closer to the surface?
Ordering Integers.answer: −150m is closer to the surface, since −150 is greater than −300 (closer to zero).

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange these account balances in ascending order: +100, −50, +25, −200.
Among the integers 0, −1, and 1, which is the smallest and which is the largest?
Ordering Integers.answer: −1 is the smallest, and 1 is the largest, with 0 sitting exactly in between them.

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange these account balances in descending order: +100, −50, +25, −200.
Why does zero sit exactly between negative and positive integers when ordering them?
Ordering Integers.answer: Because zero is neither positive nor negative — it is the reference point that separates the two groups, with all negatives to its left and all positives to its right.

Ordering Integers.q: Four hikers are at +200m, −80m, +450m, −30m. Who is at the LOWEST elevation?
Ordering Integers.answer: The hiker at −80m, since it is the smallest (most negative) value among the four.

Ordering Integers.q: Four hikers are at +200m, −80m, +450m, −30m. Who is at the HIGHEST elevation?
Ordering Integers.answer: The hiker at +450m, since it is the largest value among the four.

Ordering Integers.q: A list of temperatures reads: −15, 8, −3, 0, 20. Arrange this list in ascending order.
A list of temperatures reads: −15, 8, −3, 0, 20. Arrange this list in descending order.
Explain step by step how to determine which of two negative integers is greater, using −18 and −7 as an example.
steps: Compare the two integers’ distances from zero, ignoring their signs: 18 and 7.
Recognize that for NEGATIVE integers, a SMALLER distance from zero means a GREATER (less negative) value.
Since 7 is a smaller distance than 18, the integer −7 is greater than −18.
Ordering Integers.answer: Since −7 has a smaller distance from zero (7) than −18 (distance 18), and smaller distance means greater value for negatives, −7 > −18.

Ordering Integers.q: A class records the coldest temperature of the year as −22°C and the warmest as +38°C. What is true about comparing these two values?
Ordering Integers.answer: +38°C is far greater than −22°C, since any positive value is always greater than any negative value, and the actual gap between them (in degrees) is 60.

Ordering Integers.q: A video game leaderboard shows scores: −50, 200, 0, −10, 150. Arrange these in descending order (best score first).
A video game leaderboard shows scores: −50, 200, 0, −10, 150. Which score is the WORST?
Ordering Integers.answer: −50, since it is the smallest (most negative) value.

Ordering Integers.q: Why might a teacher use the phrase "climbing up the number line" to help students remember what ascending order means?
Ordering Integers.answer: Because ascending order moves from smaller to larger values, just like climbing UP a staircase moves you from a lower step to a higher one, creating a helpful physical/visual analogy for the concept.

Ordering Integers.q: Why might a teacher use the phrase "walking down the number line" to help students remember what descending order means?
Ordering Integers.answer: Because descending order moves from larger to smaller values, just like walking DOWN a staircase moves you from a higher step to a lower one, mirroring the direction of the ordering.

Ordering Integers.q: A list of elevation readings includes: −500, −500, 100, −200. Are there any EQUAL values in this list, and how would you handle them when ordering?
Ordering Integers.answer: Yes, there are two −500 readings, which are equal to each other; when ordering, equal values are simply placed next to each other (in either order, since they are the same), such as: −500, −500, −200, 100.

Ordering Integers.q: A list of 5 numbers needs to be put in order, but one of the numbers is written incorrectly without its negative sign (e.g., "8" was meant to be "−8"). How would this mistake affect the final ordering?
Ordering Integers.answer: Without the negative sign, the number would be mistakenly treated as a large POSITIVE value instead of a negative one, likely causing it to be placed at the wrong end of the ordered list (e.g., placed among the largest values instead of among the smallest).

Ordering Integers.q: A number line based competition ranks players by their integer scores, with the WINNER having the HIGHEST score. Player scores are: −5, 12, −20, 8, 0. Who wins, and who comes in last place?
Ordering Integers.answer: The player with 12 wins (highest score), and the player with −20 comes in last place (lowest score).

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange the following list of mixed integers in ascending order: 0, −1, 1, −100, 100, −50, 50.
Arrange the following list of mixed integers in descending order: 0, −1, 1, −100, 100, −50, 50.
A weather app shows hourly temperature readings: −2, −2, −5, 1, −5, 3. Are there any repeated values, and what does this tell you about the ordering process?
Ordering Integers.answer: Yes, −2 appears twice and −5 appears twice; when ordering, repeated (equal) values are simply grouped together at their correct position, since they are equal to themselves: −5, −5, −2, −2, 1, 3.

Ordering Integers.q: A number line shows 6 integers plotted. Without knowing their exact values, how can you quickly identify the SMALLEST one just by looking at the number line?
Ordering Integers.answer: The smallest integer will always be the one positioned FURTHEST TO THE LEFT among all the plotted points.

Ordering Integers.q: A number line shows 6 integers plotted. Without knowing their exact values, how can you quickly identify the LARGEST one just by looking at the number line?
Ordering Integers.answer: The largest integer will always be the one positioned FURTHEST TO THE RIGHT among all the plotted points.

Ordering Integers.q: A multinational company compares quarterly profits/losses (in millions of rupees) across 5 regions: North +12, South −8, East +25, West −15, Central +3. Rank these regions from BEST performing to WORST performing.
Ordering Integers.answer: East (+25) → North (+12) → Central (+3) → South (−8) → West (−15), from best to worst.

Ordering Integers.q: A climate scientist studies historical temperature extremes across 6 cities, recorded as integers: City A −40, City B +50, City C −5, City D +15, City E −25, City F 0. Arrange these cities in ascending order of their recorded extreme temperatures.
Ordering Integers.answer: City A (−40) → City E (−25) → City C (−5) → City F (0) → City D (+15) → City B (+50), from smallest to largest.

Ordering Integers.q: Explain step by step how a teacher might design a foolproof method for students to order a LARGE list of mixed positive and negative integers (say, 15 numbers) without making sign-related mistakes.
steps: First, sort the numbers into three separate groups: negative integers, zero (if present), and positive integers.
Within the negative group, order them by their distance from zero, placing the LARGEST distance (most negative) first, working toward the smallest distance (closest to zero).
Place zero next, if it exists in the list.
Within the positive group, order them normally from smallest to largest.
Finally, combine all three groups in sequence (negatives, then zero, then positives) to get the complete ascending order.
Ordering Integers.answer: Separate into negative, zero, and positive groups; order negatives from most negative to least negative, then zero, then positives from smallest to largest; combine all three groups for the full ascending order.

Ordering Integers.q: A financial analyst needs to rank 8 different investment portfolios by their annual returns (as integers, in thousands of rupees): +45, −12, +78, −30, +5, −60, +22, 0. Identify the portfolio with the SECOND-BEST performance.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ordering from best to worst: +78, +45, +22, +5, 0, −12, −30, −60. The second-best is +45.

Ordering Integers.q: A satellite tracking system records altitude changes (as integers, in km, relative to a baseline orbit) for 6 different objects: +120, −45, +200, −90, +15, −180. If objects with MORE NEGATIVE values are considered at higher "risk" of orbital decay, rank these objects from HIGHEST risk to LOWEST risk.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ranking from most negative (highest risk) to least negative/most positive (lowest risk): −180, −90, −45, +15, +120, +200.

Ordering Integers.q: Why might simply looking at the NUMBER OF DIGITS in a list of integers (ignoring their signs) lead to a completely WRONG ordering, using the example list: −500, 50, −5, 5000?
Ordering Integers.answer: Looking only at digit count (ignoring signs) might suggest 5000 (4 digits) is "biggest" and −5 (1 digit, ignoring sign) is "smallest," which happens to align here, but −500 (3 digits) would incorrectly seem bigger than 50 (2 digits) by digit-count alone, when in TRUE integer value, 50 is actually greater than −500; correctly ordering by actual value gives: −500, −5, 50, 5000.

Ordering Integers.q: A school science fair ranks projects using a combined integer score (positive for strengths, negative for weaknesses identified by judges): Project A +15, Project B −8, Project C +22, Project D −3, Project E +1. Determine the FINAL ranking from BEST to WORST.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ranking from best to worst: Project C (+22), Project A (+15), Project E (+1), Project D (−3), Project B (−8).

Ordering Integers.q: A mountain range’s peaks and valleys are recorded as integer elevations (in metres, relative to a regional baseline): Peak 1 +3200, Valley 1 −150, Peak 2 +2800, Valley 2 −400, Peak 3 +3500. Identify which valley is DEEPER (more negative) and confirm using integer comparison.
Ordering Integers.answer: Valley 2 (−400) is deeper than Valley 1 (−150), since −400 is a smaller (more negative) integer value than −150.

Ordering Integers.q: A data scientist is asked to find the MEDIAN (middle value when ordered) of this list of integers: −12, 8, −3, 15, −7, 0, 4. First, order the list, then identify the median.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ordered ascending: −12, −7, −3, 0, 4, 8, 15. With 7 values, the median (4th value) is 0.

Ordering Integers.q: A robotics competition scores 9 teams with integers: +45, −10, +30, −25, +60, 0, −5, +15, −40. Find the RANGE of scores (highest minus lowest) after ordering them.

Why might understanding both "ordering" (arranging in sequence) AND "comparing" (using > and < symbols) be considered two sides of the SAME underlying skill, rather than two completely separate topics?
Ordering Integers.answer: Both skills rely on the exact same core understanding — knowing the relative position of integers on a number line — ordering simply applies repeated pairwise comparisons (using > or <) to arrange an entire list correctly, so mastering comparison directly enables successful ordering.

Ordering Integers.q: A multinational logistics company tracks delivery delays (positive integers) and early arrivals (negative integers, in hours) for 7 shipments: +3, −2, +8, −5, 0, +1, −10. Which shipment arrived the MOST early, and which was the MOST delayed?
Ordering Integers.answer: The shipment with −10 arrived the most early (10 hours ahead of schedule), and the shipment with +8 was the most delayed (8 hours behind schedule).

Ordering Integers.q: A list of integers represents daily stock price CHANGES (not actual prices) over 10 days: +5, −3, +8, −12, +2, 0, −7, +15, −1, +4. After ordering this list in ascending order, what is the SUM of the three SMALLEST values?
Ordering Integers.answer: Ordered ascending: −12, −7, −3, −1, 0, +2, +4, +5, +8, +15. The three smallest are −12, −7, −3, summing to −12+(−7)+(−3) = −22.

Ordering Integers.q: A weather monitoring network compares the coldest recorded temperature across 5 different decades (as integers in °C): 1980s: −35, 1990s: −28, 2000s: −22, 2010s: −31, 2020s: −19. Which decade had the records show the LEAST extreme cold (i.e., the WARMEST of these cold records)?
Ordering Integers.answer: The 2020s had the warmest of these cold records, at −19°C, since it is the greatest (least negative) value among the five.

Ordering Integers.q: A submarine fleet tracks the depths of 6 vessels (in metres, as negative integers below sea level): Sub 1: −120, Sub 2: −450, Sub 3: −80, Sub 4: −600, Sub 5: −200, Sub 6: −15. Rank the submarines from CLOSEST to the surface to DEEPEST.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ranking from closest to surface to deepest: Sub 6 (−15), Sub 3 (−80), Sub 1 (−120), Sub 5 (−200), Sub 2 (−450), Sub 4 (−600).

Ordering Integers.q: A video game tournament tracks player point DIFFERENTIALS (points scored minus points conceded) for 8 players: +22, −5, +40, −18, +3, −30, +12, 0. If only the TOP 3 differentials qualify for the finals, which 3 players qualify?
Ordering Integers.answer: Ordering from highest to lowest: +40, +22, +12, +3, 0, −5, −18, −30. The top 3 qualifying differentials are +40, +22, and +12.

Ordering Integers.q: A class is asked: "Is it possible for a list of integers to have NO smallest value?" Under what unusual circumstance (if any) might this be true?
Ordering Integers.answer: For a FINITE list of specific integers, there will always be a smallest value, since you can always compare a finite set and find the minimum; this would only become impossible in an INFINITE list that extends without bound toward negative infinity, which is not a typical real-world scenario for a "list" of recorded data.

Ordering Integers.q: A factory compares production output changes (as integers, relative to a target) for 5 consecutive days: Day 1: +25, Day 2: −40, Day 3: +10, Day 4: −15, Day 5: +35. Rank the days from BEST (most above target) to WORST (most below target).
Ordering Integers.answer: Ranking from best to worst: Day 5 (+35), Day 1 (+25), Day 3 (+10), Day 4 (−15), Day 2 (−40).

Ordering Integers.q: A spreadsheet accidentally lists a negative number as positive (a data entry error), such as recording −85 as 85 in a list of scores meant to be ordered. How could comparing the ERRONEOUS ordered list with a CORRECTED ordered list help identify which entry was likely mistyped?
Ordering Integers.answer: If 85 appears unexpectedly high in an otherwise mostly negative or low-scoring list, that mismatch (an unusually high positive value appearing in a context where you would expect a negative one) could be a strong clue that the entry’s sign was mistakenly entered incorrectly, prompting a double-check of the original data.

Ordering Integers.q: A list of 5 city elevations (in metres, as integers) is: −10, 250, −85, 0, 1500. A geography teacher asks students to identify both the median (middle value when ordered) and the range (highest minus lowest). Find both.
Ordering Integers.answer: Ordered ascending: −85, −10, 0, 250, 1500. The median (middle value) is 0. The range is 1500 − (−85) = 1500 + 85 = 1585.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A lift starts at the 4th floor (+4) and goes down 9 floors. Write this as an addition and find where it ends up.
A submarine at −60m rises 25m. Represent this as an addition and find the new depth.
What is the additive inverse of the integer representing “a loss of ₹350”?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: “A loss of ₹350” is −350. Its additive inverse is +350.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: Which is greater: a temperature of −8°C or a temperature of −15°C? Explain using the number line.
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: −8°C is greater, since −8 is further right (closer to zero) than −15 on the number line.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A hiker is at +200m elevation. They descend 350m, then climb 100m. What is their final elevation?
Find the difference between +18 and −7 (i.e., how much more is +18 than −7?).
Order these three bank balances from smallest to largest: −₹500, +₹120, −₹50.
A diver at 0m (the surface) dives down 22m, then down another 8m. What is her final depth?
What integer represents “14°C below freezing”, and what is its additive inverse?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: “14°C below freezing” is −14. Its additive inverse is +14.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A football team’s yardage over 3 plays is: −5, +12, −3. What is the total yardage gained or lost?
Explain step by step how to solve: a lift at −2 goes up 6 floors, then down 9 floors. Where does it end up?
Which calculation finds “how many degrees warmer is 12°C than −20°C”?
A balloon at 500m descends 700m. Is it now above or below the starting reference point (0m), and by how much?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: 500 + (−700) = −200m, so it is 200m BELOW the starting reference point.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: What is the additive inverse of 0, and why does it make sense that it equals itself?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: The additive inverse of 0 is 0, because 0 + 0 = 0 — zero is the only integer that is its own additive inverse, since it sits exactly at the boundary with no direction to flip.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: Three towns have elevations +80m, −15m, and −200m. Which town is at the LOWEST elevation?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: The town at −200m, since it is the smallest (most negative) of the three values.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A video game score starts at 0. A player gains 45 points, loses 60, then gains 30. What is the final score?
Explain step by step how to find the difference between a mountain peak at +6200m and a valley at −150m.
steps: Identify this as a “difference” question, which means subtraction.
Set up the subtraction: peak minus valley = 6200 − (−150).
Subtracting a negative becomes adding a positive: 6200 + 150 = 6350.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A weather log shows temperature changes of +5, −9, +3 over one day, starting at 16°C. What is the final temperature?
Why is identifying the “zero point” the most important first step in any integer word problem?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: Every value in the problem is an integer measured RELATIVE to that zero point (like ground level, sea level, or a starting score) — without correctly identifying it, you cannot correctly assign positive or negative signs to anything in the problem.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A scuba diver at −9m rises 4m, then the additive inverse of that rise is applied as a NEW dive. What is her final depth?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: Rising 4m: (−9) + 4 = −5m. The additive inverse of +4 is −4, applied as a new dive: (−5) + (−4) = −9m — she ends back at her original depth.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A delivery van travels +85km from a depot, then −85km. Using the idea of additive inverse, explain why it ends up exactly back at the depot.
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.answer: +85 and −85 are additive inverses of each other, so their sum is always 0: 85 + (−85) = 0, meaning the van returns to exactly its starting position (the depot).

Types of Fractions.q: What is a fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: A fraction is a number that represents a part of a whole.

Types of Fractions.q: What is the numerator of a fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: The numerator is the top number, showing how many equal parts are being considered.

Types of Fractions.q: What is the denominator of a fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: The denominator is the bottom number, showing the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into.

Types of Fractions.q: In the fraction 5/8, identify the numerator and denominator.
Types of Fractions.answer: Numerator = 5, Denominator = 8.

Types of Fractions.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. If you eat 2 slices, what fraction of the pizza did you eat?
Types of Fractions.answer: 2/6 of the pizza.

Types of Fractions.q: A cake is cut into 10 equal pieces. If 4 pieces are given away, what fraction is given away?
Types of Fractions.answer: 4/10 of the cake.

Types of Fractions.q: Why must the parts of a whole be equal for a fraction to make sense?
Types of Fractions.answer: Because a fraction assumes each part represents the same-sized share — if parts were unequal, the numerator would not fairly represent the portion taken.

Types of Fractions.q: Can a fraction describe part of a group of objects, like marbles in a bag? Explain.
Types of Fractions.answer: Yes — a fraction can represent part of any whole, including a collection. For example, if 3 out of 10 marbles are blue, that is 3/10 of the marbles.

Types of Fractions.q: A basket has 9 fruits. If 4 are bananas, what fraction of the fruits are bananas?
Types of Fractions.answer: 4/9 of the fruits are bananas.

Types of Fractions.q: A class has 40 students. If 25 are boys, what fraction of the class are boys?
Types of Fractions.answer: 25/40 of the class are boys.

Types of Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to find what fraction of a chocolate bar (12 equal pieces) is left if 5 pieces are eaten.
steps: Find the total number of equal pieces: 12.
Find the number of pieces left: 12−5=7.
Write the fraction: pieces left over total pieces = 7/12.
Types of Fractions.answer: 7/12 of the chocolate bar is left.

Types of Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to find what fraction of a 20-page notebook has been written on, if 13 pages are filled.
steps: Find the total number of pages: 20.
Find the number of filled pages: 13.
Write the fraction: filled pages over total pages = 13/20.
Types of Fractions.answer: 13/20 of the notebook has been written on.

Types of Fractions.q: A garden has 18 plants, and 11 of them have flowered. What fraction of the plants have NOT flowered?
Types of Fractions.answer: 18−11=7 plants have not flowered, so the fraction is 7/18.

Types of Fractions.q: Why is 5/5 considered to represent one whole, even though it is written as a fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: Because the numerator (5) equals the denominator (5), meaning all equal parts of the whole are included — and including every part makes one complete whole.

Types of Fractions.q: A train has 14 coaches, and 6 are reserved for sleeper class. What fraction of the coaches are reserved for sleeper class?
Types of Fractions.answer: 6/14 of the coaches are reserved for sleeper class.

Types of Fractions.q: A box has 16 chocolates, and all 16 are dark chocolate. What fraction of the box is dark chocolate?
Types of Fractions.answer: 16/16, which represents the whole box (equal to 1).

Types of Fractions.q: Why does the order matter in a fraction — that is, why is 3/8 different from 8/3?
Types of Fractions.answer: In 3/8, we take 3 parts out of a whole divided into 8 equal parts (less than 1 whole). In 8/3, we would be taking 8 parts where the whole is divided into only 3 parts (more than 2 wholes) — these represent very different amounts.

Types of Fractions.q: A library has 50 books, and 22 are storybooks. What fraction of the books are storybooks?
Types of Fractions.answer: 22/50 of the books are storybooks.

Types of Fractions.q: A jar of 24 candies has 9 red candies and the rest are yellow. What fraction of the candies are yellow?
Types of Fractions.answer: 24−9=15 candies are yellow, so the fraction is 15/24.

Types of Fractions.q: A shape is divided into 7 equal parts. What is the denominator if we want to write a fraction for this shape?
Types of Fractions.answer: 7, since the whole is divided into 7 equal parts.

Types of Fractions.q: If 4 out of 7 equal parts of a shape are shaded, what fraction is shaded?
Types of Fractions.answer: 4/7 is shaded.

Types of Fractions.q: A rectangle is divided into 5 equal vertical strips. If 3 strips are colored blue, what fraction is blue?
Types of Fractions.answer: 3/5 of the rectangle is blue.

Types of Fractions.q: A water bottle is marked into 4 equal sections. If water fills up to 3 sections, what fraction of the bottle is full?
Types of Fractions.answer: 3/4 of the bottle is full.

Types of Fractions.q: A farmer has 30 hens, and 18 of them are brown. What fraction of the hens are brown?
Types of Fractions.answer: 18/30 of the hens are brown.

Types of Fractions.q: A test has 25 questions, and a student answered 21 correctly. What fraction of the questions were answered correctly?
Types of Fractions.answer: 21/25 of the questions were answered correctly.

Types of Fractions.q: Why is identifying the numerator and denominator correctly so important when writing a fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: Swapping them changes the meaning entirely — the numerator must always represent the parts being counted, and the denominator the total equal parts, otherwise the fraction misrepresents the actual portion.

Types of Fractions.q: A school has 200 students, and 85 of them participate in sports. What fraction of the students participate in sports?
Types of Fractions.answer: 85/200 of the students participate in sports.

Types of Fractions.q: A wall is painted in 6 equal sections, and 1 section remains unpainted. What fraction of the wall is unpainted?
Types of Fractions.answer: 1/6 of the wall is unpainted.

Types of Fractions.q: A road trip of 9 equal-distance stages has been completed for 5 stages. What fraction of the trip remains?
Types of Fractions.answer: 9−5=4 stages remain, so the fraction is 4/9.

Types of Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to find what fraction of a 15-item shopping list has been purchased, if 11 items are bought.
steps: Identify the total number of items: 15.
Identify the number of items purchased: 11.
Write the fraction: purchased items over total items = 11/15.
Types of Fractions.answer: 11/15 of the shopping list has been purchased.

Types of Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to find what fraction of a 60-minute movie remains, if 22 minutes have already played.
steps: Write the fraction: remaining minutes over total minutes = 38/60.
Types of Fractions.answer: 38/60 of the movie remains.

Types of Fractions.q: A fruit seller has 45 mangoes, and sells 19 of them. What fraction of the mangoes are NOT sold?
Types of Fractions.answer: 45−19=26 mangoes are not sold, so the fraction is 26/45.

Types of Fractions.q: Why can a fraction never have a denominator of 0?
Types of Fractions.answer: A denominator of 0 would mean the whole is divided into 0 parts, which is meaningless — division by zero is undefined, so a fraction must always have a non-zero denominator.

Types of Fractions.q: A jar has 100 marbles, all of which are glass marbles. What fraction of the jar is glass marbles?
Types of Fractions.answer: 100/100, representing the entire jar (equal to 1 whole).

Types of Fractions.q: A choir has 32 singers, and 14 are sopranos. What fraction of the choir are NOT sopranos?
Types of Fractions.answer: 32−14=18 are not sopranos, so the fraction is 18/32.

Types of Fractions.q: A 12-month calendar shows 5 months have passed. What fraction of the year has passed?
Types of Fractions.answer: 5/12 of the year has passed.

Types of Fractions.q: Why might a recipe use fractions, like 3/4 cup of sugar, instead of describing amounts in whole cups only?
Types of Fractions.answer: Fractions allow for more precise measurements that fall between whole numbers, which is essential for recipes that need exact amounts smaller than a full cup.

Types of Fractions.q: A parking lot has 75 cars, and 48 are sedans. What fraction of the cars in the lot are sedans?
Types of Fractions.answer: 48/75 of the cars are sedans.

Types of Fractions.q: A survey of 80 people found that 52 prefer tea over coffee. What fraction of people prefer tea?
Types of Fractions.answer: 52/80 prefer tea.

Types of Fractions.q: In a fraction a/b, why must "a" and "b" both be whole numbers (with b not equal to 0) for it to be a simple fraction?
Types of Fractions.answer: Because a fraction represents counting whole equal parts (numerator) out of a whole number of total equal divisions (denominator); a non-zero whole number denominator ensures the whole is meaningfully divided.

Types of Fractions.q: A company has 120 employees, and 75 work in the sales department. What fraction of employees work in sales?
Types of Fractions.answer: 75/120 work in the sales department.

Types of Fractions.q: A 500ml bottle has 235ml of juice remaining. Thinking of the bottle in terms of equal "units" (ml), what fraction of the bottle (out of 500) is filled?
Types of Fractions.answer: 235/500 of the bottle is filled.

Types of Fractions.q: Why is the fraction 0/5 a valid fraction, even though the numerator is 0?
Types of Fractions.answer: A numerator of 0 simply means none of the parts are being counted — it represents nothing out of the 5 equal parts, which is still a meaningful (though minimal) quantity, equal to 0.

Types of Fractions.q: A charity collected donations from 90 households, and 63 households donated. What fraction of households donated?
Types of Fractions.answer: 63/90 of households donated.

Types of Fractions.q: A 28-day month has had rain on 9 days. What fraction of the days have had rain, and what fraction have NOT had rain?
Types of Fractions.answer: 9/28 of days had rain; 28−9=19 days did not, so 19/28 did not have rain.

Types of Fractions.q: Why can two different real-world situations (like "3 out of 4 pizza slices eaten" and "3 out of 4 students passing") both be represented using the exact same fraction, 3/4?
Types of Fractions.answer: A fraction is an abstract mathematical idea representing a ratio of parts to a whole — it does not depend on what the "whole" physically is, so the same fraction 3/4 can apply to pizza slices, students, or any other countable whole.

Types of Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to determine what fraction of a 36-item collection of stamps is from foreign countries, if 27 stamps are foreign.
steps: Identify the total number of stamps: 36.
Identify the number of foreign stamps: 27.
Write the fraction: foreign stamps over total stamps = 27/36.
Types of Fractions.answer: 27/36 of the stamps are from foreign countries.

Types of Fractions.q: A water tank holding 1000 litres currently has 640 litres. What fraction of the tank’s capacity is filled, and what fraction is empty?
A baker prepares 48 cupcakes for a sale, and by the end of the day, 39 have been sold. What fraction remain unsold?
Types of Fractions.answer: 48−39=9 remain unsold, so the fraction is 9/48.

Types of Fractions.q: Why might understanding fractions of a collection be especially useful for understanding statistics, like "3 out of 5 doctors recommend"?
Types of Fractions.answer: Such statistics are essentially fractions of a collection (in this case, doctors), and understanding how fractions represent parts of a group helps interpret these statements accurately as proportions rather than absolute numbers.

Types of Fractions.q: A spelling test has 40 words, and a student spelled 33 correctly. What fraction of words were spelled correctly, and what fraction were incorrect?
Types of Fractions.answer: 33/40 correct; 40−33=7, so 7/40 incorrect.

Types of Fractions.q: Why is it important that the denominator of a fraction describing a real collection (like students in a class) matches the ACTUAL total count of that collection?
Types of Fractions.answer: If the denominator does not match the true total, the fraction would misrepresent the actual proportion — for example, saying "10/20 students passed" when there are really 30 students would give an inaccurate picture of how many passed.

Types of Fractions.q: A theatre has 250 seats, and during a show, 210 seats are occupied. What fraction of seats are empty?
Types of Fractions.answer: 250−210=40 seats are empty, so the fraction is 40/250.

Types of Fractions.q: A bag of 56 toffees has 23 strawberry-flavoured toffees. What fraction of toffees are NOT strawberry-flavoured?
Types of Fractions.answer: 56−23=33 are not strawberry, so the fraction is 33/56.

Types of Fractions.q: Why can the same physical object (like a single pizza) be described using completely different fractions depending on how many EQUAL pieces it is cut into?
Types of Fractions.answer: Because the denominator changes based on the number of equal parts chosen for cutting; eating the same amount of pizza could be 1/2 if cut into 2 pieces, but 4/8 if cut into 8 pieces — the fraction depends on the chosen division, not just the amount eaten.

Types of Fractions.q: A 90-question exam paper has 72 multiple-choice questions, and the rest are descriptive. What fraction of the paper is descriptive questions?
Types of Fractions.answer: 90−72=18 are descriptive, so the fraction is 18/90.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: What is a proper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: A proper fraction is one where the numerator is smaller than the denominator, representing a value less than 1.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: What is an improper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: An improper fraction is one where the numerator is greater than or equal to the denominator, representing a value of 1 or more.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: What is a mixed fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: A mixed fraction combines a whole number with a proper fraction, like 2 1/3.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Is 4/9 a proper or improper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Proper, since the numerator (4) is smaller than the denominator (9).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Is 11/6 a proper or improper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Improper, since the numerator (11) is greater than the denominator (6).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Convert 9/4 into a mixed fraction.
Convert 13/5 into a mixed fraction.
Convert the mixed fraction 2 3/4 into an improper fraction.
Convert the mixed fraction 5 1/3 into an improper fraction.
Explain step by step how to convert the improper fraction 17/5 into a mixed fraction.
steps: The quotient (3) becomes the whole number part.
The remainder over the divisor (2/5) becomes the fraction part.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Explain step by step how to convert the mixed fraction 4 2/7 into an improper fraction.
steps: Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 4×7=28.
Keep the same denominator: the result is 30/7.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Why is the fraction 6/6 classified as an improper fraction even though it equals exactly 1?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Because the rule for improper fractions is that the numerator is greater than OR EQUAL TO the denominator — since 6 equals 6, it satisfies this rule, even though the value is exactly 1, not more than 1.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Why does every whole number, like 5, have an equivalent improper fraction form?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Any whole number can be written as a fraction with itself as a multiple of the denominator — for example, 5 = 5/1, or 5 = 10/2, or 5 = 15/3, since multiplying numerator and denominator equally keeps the same value.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Write the whole number 7 as an improper fraction with denominator 3.
A recipe calls for 7/2 cups of milk. Express this as a mixed fraction.
A ribbon measures 19/4 metres long. Express this length as a mixed fraction.
Why is converting an improper fraction to a mixed fraction often more useful in everyday situations, like measuring cloth or ingredients?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: A mixed fraction (like 3 1/2 metres) is often easier to visualize and communicate practically than a large improper fraction (like 7/2 metres), since the whole number part immediately tells you how many full units are involved.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A juice container holds 23/6 litres. Express this as a mixed fraction.
Convert 5 3/8 into an improper fraction.
Convert 21/8 into a mixed fraction.
Why must the fraction part of a mixed number always be a PROPER fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: If the fraction part were improper or equal to 1, it would mean there is at least one more whole unit hidden in the fraction part, which should instead be added to the whole number part for a correctly simplified mixed fraction.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A bag of flour weighs 27/4 kg. Express this as a mixed fraction.
A carpenter cuts wood pieces totalling 31/6 metres. Express this length as a mixed fraction.
Convert the mixed fraction 6 5/9 into an improper fraction.
A painter mixed 8 2/5 litres of paint. Express this as an improper fraction.
Why might engineers or scientists often prefer to use improper fractions (rather than mixed fractions) when doing calculations?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Improper fractions are a single, complete fraction form that is easier to use directly in multiplication, division, or other calculations, without needing to separately handle whole number and fraction parts as you would with a mixed fraction.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A tank contains 38/7 litres of fuel. Express this as a mixed fraction.
Explain step by step how to determine whether 29/4 is a proper or improper fraction, and convert it to a mixed fraction if needed.
steps: Compare numerator (29) and denominator (4): since 29 > 4, this is an improper fraction.
Write the mixed fraction: whole number 7, fraction part 1/4.
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: 29/4 is improper, and as a mixed fraction it is 7 1/4.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A jug contains 33/5 litres of milk. How many WHOLE litres of milk are there, and what fraction is left over?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: 33÷5=6 remainder 3, so there are 6 whole litres, with 3/5 litre left over (6 3/5 litres total).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Why is 0/4 considered a proper fraction, even though its value is 0?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: Since the numerator (0) is less than the denominator (4), it fits the definition of a proper fraction — having a numerator smaller than the denominator — even though the actual value represented is zero.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A construction project uses 47/8 tonnes of cement. Express this as a mixed fraction.
Convert the mixed fraction 9 1/6 into an improper fraction.
A 3 1/2 hour movie is being timed in minutes using fractions of an hour. Express 3 1/2 as an improper fraction.
Why does the denominator stay UNCHANGED both when converting mixed-to-improper and improper-to-mixed?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: The denominator represents the SIZE of each equal part of the whole — this size does not change during conversion, only how we GROUP and COUNT those parts (as a whole number plus leftover, or as one big count) changes.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A water tank stores 52/9 thousand litres. Express this as a mixed fraction.
A bakery uses 63/8 kg of flour across several batches. Express this as a mixed fraction, showing your steps.
A relay race has runners covering a TOTAL distance written as the improper fraction 44/7 km. If converted to a mixed fraction, what does the whole number part tell us about the race?
Proper & Improper Fractions.answer: 44÷7=6 remainder 2, so 44/7=6 2/7 km — the whole number 6 tells us the race covered at least 6 FULL kilometres, with an extra 2/7 km beyond that.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Two mixed fractions, 3 1/4 and 13/4, are claimed to be equal. Verify this by converting 3 1/4 to an improper fraction.
