Tenths & Hundredths.q: On a number line from 0 to 1 split into tenths, where does 0.4 sit?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 0.4 sits four-tenths of the way between 0 and 1.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Write 1/10 and 1/100 as decimals.
In the decimal 8.93, which digit is in the whole number place and which is in the tenths place?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 8 is the whole number, 9 is in the tenths place.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A pizza is cut into 100 equal slices, and 12 are eaten. Write the fraction eaten as a decimal.
Why are decimal place values (tenths, hundredths) each ten times smaller than the one before?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: Just like whole number places grow ten times bigger moving left (ones, tens, hundreds), decimal places shrink ten times smaller moving right after the point — each new place divides the previous one by 10.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Write 0.06 as a fraction.
A garden bed is divided into 10 equal rows, and 2 rows have flowers. Write this as a decimal.
Write 7/10 as a decimal.
Write 81/100 as a decimal.
In the decimal 3.05, which digit is in the tenths place and which is in the hundredths place?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 0 is in the tenths place, 5 is in the hundredths place.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A strip of 10 equal boxes has 9 shaded. Write this as a decimal.
A 10x10 grid has 50 squares shaded. Write this as a decimal.
Read the decimal 2.7 in words.
Read the decimal 0.19 in words.
What is the whole number part of 100.4?
Write 1/100 as a decimal in words.
Why does the second digit after the decimal point represent hundredths, not tenths?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: The first digit after the point represents tenths (a whole split into 10), and the second digit represents a further split into 10, making each part a hundredth (1/100) of the original whole.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A 10x10 grid has 99 squares shaded. Write this as a decimal.
Explain step by step how to write "3 shaded squares out of a 10x10 grid" as a decimal.
steps: Convert to decimal with 2 digits after the point: 0.03.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Read the decimal 0.5 in words, and explain what it equals as a fraction.
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: Read as "zero point five"; it equals the fraction 5/10 (or 1/2).

Tenths & Hundredths.q: On a number line from 0 to 1 split into tenths, where does 0.9 sit?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 0.9 sits nine-tenths of the way between 0 and 1, very close to 1.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Write 6/10 as a decimal.
Write 14/100 as a decimal.
In the decimal 0.27, which digit is in the tenths place?
In the decimal 0.27, which digit is in the hundredths place?
A strip of 10 equal boxes has 1 shaded. Write this as a decimal.
A 10x10 grid has 75 squares shaded. Write this as a decimal.
Why is the decimal 0.3 the same as the fraction 3/10?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: The single digit after the decimal point represents tenths, so 0.3 means 3 tenths, exactly the same as the fraction 3/10.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Read the decimal 11.06 in words.
Write 8/10 as a decimal.
Write 3/100 as a decimal.
What is the decimal part of 42.18?
A class survey shows 40 out of 100 students like cricket. Write this as a decimal.
Explain step by step how to convert "60 shaded squares out of 100" into a decimal.
steps: Convert: since there are 2 zeros in 100, write 2 digits after the point: 0.60.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Why might 0.6 and 0.60 represent the exact same point on a number line divided into hundredths?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 0.6 equals 0.60 since the trailing zero adds no extra value — both mark the same position, six-tenths (or sixty-hundredths) of the way from 0 to 1.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A 10x10 grid has 8 squares shaded. Write this as both a fraction and a decimal.
Read the decimal 0.02 in words.
Write the decimal 0.1 as a fraction with denominator 10.
A ribbon is cut into 10 equal strips, and all 10 are used. Write this as a decimal.
On a number line from 0 to 1 split into hundredths, roughly where does 0.25 sit?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: 0.25 sits a quarter of the way (twenty-five hundredths) between 0 and 1.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Why is understanding tenths and hundredths important before learning to add or subtract decimals?
Tenths & Hundredths.answer: Knowing what each decimal place represents helps you correctly line up digits by place value when adding or subtracting, avoiding errors from mismatched tenths and hundredths.

Comparing Decimals.q: Are 0.6 and 0.60 the same value? Explain.
Comparing Decimals.answer: Yes — they are equivalent decimals. Adding a zero at the end of the decimal part does not change its value.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.25 to a fraction.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 25/100 (which simplifies to 1/4).

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 4/10 to a decimal.
Which is greater: 7.3 or 7.29?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 7.3 is greater, since 7.30 has a 3 in the tenths place, which is more than 2 in 7.29.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from smallest to largest: 1.2, 1.02, 1.22.
Why do trailing zeros not change a decimal\u2019s value, but a zero placed elsewhere can?
Comparing Decimals.answer: A trailing zero (at the very end) adds an empty smaller place value, which represents nothing extra. But a zero placed before other digits (like turning 0.5 into 0.05) changes which place each digit occupies, so it does change the value.

Comparing Decimals.q: Write an equivalent decimal for 0.8 with two decimal digits.
Convert 0.6 to a fraction.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 6/10 (which simplifies to 3/5).

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 9/100 to a decimal.
Which is smaller: 2.4 or 2.04?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 2.04 is smaller, since comparing tenths, 0 < 4.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from largest to smallest: 6.5, 6.05, 6.55.
Is 0.3 equal to 0.30 and 0.300?
Comparing Decimals.answer: Yes, all three are equivalent decimals representing the same value.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.7 to a fraction.
Convert 19/100 to a decimal.
Which is greater: 0.5 or 0.49?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 0.5 is greater, since 0.50 has tenths digit 5, more than 4 in 0.49.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from smallest to largest: 3.1, 3.11, 3.01.
Explain step by step how to compare 6.45 and 6.5.
steps: Give both the same decimal digits: 6.45 and 6.50.
Compare tenths digits: 5 > 4, so 6.5 is greater.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 6.5 is greater than 6.45.

Comparing Decimals.q: Two friends measure rainfall: 3.4 cm and 3.04 cm. Whose measurement is greater?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 3.4 cm is greater, since comparing tenths, 4 > 0.

Comparing Decimals.q: Why is comparing 12.8 and 9.99 simple, without even checking the decimal digits?
Comparing Decimals.answer: Because the whole number parts already differ (12 vs 9), and 12 is greater than 9, so 12.8 must be greater regardless of the decimal digits.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.45 to a fraction, and explain each step.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 0.45 has 2 decimal digits, so it becomes 45/100 (which simplifies to 9/20).

Comparing Decimals.q: Write three equivalent decimals for 0.2.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 0.2, 0.20, 0.200 are all equivalent.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.08 to a fraction.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 8/100 (which simplifies to 2/25).

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 73/100 to a decimal.
Order these decimals from largest to smallest: 0.9, 0.09, 0.19.
Why is it useful to rewrite decimals with the SAME number of decimal digits before comparing them?
Comparing Decimals.answer: It lines up each place value correctly, so you can compare tenths with tenths, hundredths with hundredths, without making mistakes from differing digit counts.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.9 to a fraction.
Convert 31/100 to a decimal.
Which is bigger: 4.06 or 4.6?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 4.6 is bigger, since 4.60 has tenths digit 6, more than 0 in 4.06.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from smallest to largest: 8.8, 8.08, 8.88.
Write an equivalent decimal for 0.4 with three decimal digits.
Convert 0.15 to a fraction.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 15/100 (which simplifies to 3/20).

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 6/10 to a decimal.
Which is smaller: 10.2 or 10.19?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 10.19 is smaller, since comparing tenths, 1 < 2.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from largest to smallest: 1.05, 1.5, 1.15.
Explain step by step how to order 5.1, 5.11, 5.01 from smallest to largest.
steps: Rewrite with the same decimal digits: 5.10, 5.11, 5.01.
Compare hundredths since tenths may tie: 5.01 has tenths digit 0, smallest.
Then 5.10 (tenths 1, hundredths 0) is next, and 5.11 (tenths 1, hundredths 1) is largest.

Comparing Decimals.q: A shop sells two ropes: 8.6 m and 8.65 m. Which rope is shorter?
Comparing Decimals.answer: The 8.6 m rope is shorter, since 8.60 < 8.65 when comparing hundredths.

Comparing Decimals.q: Why can a decimal like 0.7 be both "bigger" than 0.65 in value, even though 65 looks like a bigger number than 7?
Comparing Decimals.answer: Decimals must be compared by place value, not by treating the digits after the point as a whole number. 0.7 = 0.70, and comparing to 0.65, the tenths digit 7 is greater than 6, making 0.7 the bigger value overall — the digit count after the point does not matter.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.03 to a fraction.
Convert 8/100 to a decimal.
Which is greater: 13.4 or 13.39?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 13.4 is greater, since 13.40 has tenths digit 4, more than 3 in 13.39.

Comparing Decimals.q: Are 1.5 and 1.500 equivalent decimals?
Comparing Decimals.answer: Yes, both represent the same value, one and a half.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.12 to a fraction.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 12/100 (which simplifies to 3/25).

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 2/10 to a decimal.
Which is greater: 5.05 or 5.5?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 5.5 is greater, since 5.50 has tenths digit 5, more than 0 in 5.05.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from smallest to largest: 9.9, 9.09, 9.99.
Write an equivalent decimal for 0.05 with three decimal digits.
Convert 0.99 to a fraction.
Convert 56/100 to a decimal.
Which is smaller: 3.33 or 3.3?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 3.3 (3.30) is smaller, since comparing hundredths, 0 < 3.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order these decimals from largest to smallest: 7.07, 7.7, 7.77.
Why does 4.2 equal 4.20 but NOT equal 4.02?
Comparing Decimals.answer: 4.20 just adds a trailing zero to 4.2, keeping the same value. But 4.02 shifts the 2 into the hundredths place instead of the tenths place, changing the actual value to something smaller.

Comparing Decimals.q: Convert 0.4 to a fraction with denominator 10.
A baker uses 2.25 kg of flour for one cake and 2.5 kg for another. Which cake used more flour?
Comparing Decimals.answer: The second cake (2.5 kg, written as 2.50 kg) used more flour, since 50 > 25 when comparing hundredths.

Comparing Decimals.q: Explain step by step how to compare 0.08 and 0.8.
steps: Both have a whole number part of 0.
Rewrite with the same digits: 0.08 and 0.80.
Compare tenths: 8 (in 0.80) is much greater than 0 (in 0.08).
Comparing Decimals.answer: 0.8 is much greater than 0.08.

Comparing Decimals.q: Why is it a common mistake to think 0.25 is smaller than 0.9 just because "25" looks bigger than "9"?
Comparing Decimals.answer: Comparing decimals is not the same as comparing the digits after the point as whole numbers — you must compare place by place. 0.9 (0.90) has a tenths digit of 9, which beats the tenths digit of 2 in 0.25, so 0.9 is actually bigger.

Comparing Decimals.q: Order three rainfall readings: 12.5 mm, 12.05 mm, 12.55 mm from smallest to largest.
Convert 0.07 to a fraction, and explain why a zero is needed.
Comparing Decimals.answer: 0.07 = 7/100. A zero is needed in the tenths place because there are zero full tenths, only 7 hundredths.

Comparing Decimals.q: Why is finding equivalent decimals (like 0.5 = 0.50) a useful skill before comparing or ordering decimals?
Comparing Decimals.answer: It lets you give every decimal the same number of digits after the point, which makes place-by-place comparison accurate and avoids confusing fewer digits with a smaller value.

Comparing Decimals.q: A runner completes a race in 14.3 seconds, another in 14.28 seconds. Who was faster?
Comparing Decimals.answer: The runner with 14.28 seconds was faster, since comparing hundredths after matching digits (14.30 vs 14.28), 28 < 30 means less time taken.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: Because there are exactly 100 paise in a rupee, so 2 decimal digits are needed to represent the paise part accurately — just like hundredths.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: What does the .25 mean in the price ₹56.25?

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write 7 mm using a decimal (in cm).
Write 250 cm using a decimal (in metres).
How many mm make 1 cm, and how many cm make 1 m?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: 10 mm make 1 cm, and 100 cm make 1 m.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write ₹20 and 5 paise using a decimal.
Write 12 m and 5 cm using a decimal (in metres).
A ribbon is 7 cm and 2 mm long. Write its length as a decimal in cm.
Why might writing a length like "2 m 5 cm" as 2.5 m (instead of 2.05 m) be a common mistake?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: 5 cm is only 5/100 of a metre, not 5/10 — so it must go in the hundredths place. Writing 2.5 m would actually mean 2 m 50 cm, which is ten times too much.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write ₹3 and 99 paise using a decimal.
Write 6 m and 70 cm using a decimal (in metres).
How many paise are in ₹12.50?
Write 1 cm and 9 mm using a decimal (in cm).

Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: 0.65 m = 65 cm, so the wall is 2 m and 65 cm tall.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write 3 mm using a decimal (in cm).
Write 80 cm using a decimal (in metres).

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: A road is 3.2 km long. How many metres is this (1 km = 1000 m)?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: 0.2 km = 200 m, so the road is 3000 m + 200 m = 3200 m.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Why do both money and length use decimals in a similar way?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.answer: Both have a smaller unit that fits into a bigger unit in groups of 10 or 100 (100 paise = 1 rupee, 100 cm = 1 m), so decimals naturally describe these "part of a whole unit" amounts.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write ₹65 and 1 paisa using a decimal.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: Why must decimal points be lined up before adding or subtracting decimals?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: Lining up decimal points ensures digits of the same place value (tenths with tenths, hundredths with hundredths) are added or subtracted together correctly.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: Explain step by step how to find 6.4 − 2.75.
steps: Write 6.4 as 6.40 to match decimal digits.
Line up the decimal points: 6.40 and 2.75.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: Riya buys a notebook for ₹35.50 and a pen for ₹12.75. What is the total cost, and how much change from a ₹50 note?
A jug holds 1.5 litres of juice. If 0.65 litres is poured out, how much remains?
A boy walks 1.25 km to school and 1.25 km back. How far does he walk in total?
A rope is 5 m long. If 1.8 m is cut off, how much rope remains?
A tailor has 4.5 m of cloth and uses 2.85 m for a shirt. How much cloth is left?
Why might forgetting to add a trailing zero before subtracting decimals lead to a wrong answer?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: Without matching decimal digits, the columns would not line up by place value, so you could end up subtracting a tenths digit from a hundredths digit, giving an incorrect result.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A shopkeeper sold goods worth ₹245.50 on Monday and ₹189.75 on Tuesday. What was the total sales for both days?
A water tank has 50 litres. If 18.4 litres is used in the morning and 12.65 litres in the evening, how much water remains?
Explain step by step how to add 18.07 and 5.6.
steps: Write 5.6 as 5.60 to match decimal digits.
Line up the decimal points: 18.07 and 5.60.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: In a word problem, what does the phrase 'in total' usually signal?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: It usually signals addition — combining two or more decimal quantities.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: In a word problem, what does the phrase 'how much more' usually signal?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: It usually signals subtraction — finding the difference between two decimal quantities.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A bottle has 2 litres of milk. If 0.75 litres is used for tea and 0.5 litres for coffee, how much milk is left?
A farmer harvests 12.5 kg of tomatoes on day 1 and 9.75 kg on day 2. What is the total harvest?
Why is it important to write the final answer in a decimal word problem with the CORRECT unit (like ₹ or m)?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: The number alone does not convey meaning — including the correct unit makes clear what real-world quantity (money, length, etc.) the answer represents.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A student scored 18.5 marks in Part A and 22.75 marks in Part B. What is the total score?
A bucket has 9.5 litres of water. If 3.85 litres is used, how much remains?
Explain step by step how to solve a two-step decimal word problem: a man earns ₹450.50 and spends ₹275.75, then earns another ₹50. What is his final amount?
A wire of length 7.5 m is cut into two pieces. One piece is 3.25 m. How long is the other piece?
In a word problem, what does the phrase 'combined weight' usually signal?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: It usually signals addition — adding the individual decimal weights together.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A runner ran 5.2 km on Monday and 4.85 km on Tuesday. How much further did she run on Monday than Tuesday?
A shopkeeper has ₹500. After selling goods worth ₹125.50 and buying supplies worth ₹89.25, how much money does he have?
Why is breaking a multi-step decimal word problem into smaller steps (just like with fractions) a good strategy?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: It avoids confusion by solving one operation at a time, using the result of each step as the input for the next, which is easier and less error-prone than trying to do everything at once.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A tank loses 0.15 litres of water per hour. How much water is lost after combining two readings of 0.15 litres and 0.15 litres (2 hours)?
A baker has 6 kg of sugar. He uses 2.4 kg for one batch and 1.85 kg for another. How much sugar is left?
Why does mastering decimal addition and subtraction matter for everyday life, beyond just maths class?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.answer: Many real-life tasks — handling money, measuring ingredients or materials, tracking distances — naturally involve decimal amounts, so being able to add and subtract them accurately is essential for budgeting, shopping, cooking, and similar everyday activities.

Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.q: In 6.372, name the place value of the digit 3.
In 6.372, name the place value of the digit 7.
In 6.372, name the place value of the digit 2.
What is the value of the digit 3 in 12.638?
What is the value of the digit 8 in 12.638?
Explain step by step how to expand 7.208.
Why is each decimal place value 10 times smaller than the one before it?
Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.answer: Just as whole number places grow 10 times bigger moving left (ones, tens, hundreds), decimal places shrink 10 times smaller moving right, matching how each place divides the previous one by 10.

Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.q: In the number 300.025, what is the value of the digit 5?
A price tag reads ₹156.75. Which digit represents the number of whole rupees in the tens place?
Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.answer: 5 is in the tens place, representing 50 rupees.

Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.q: Write the decimal that has 4 in the tens place, 0 in the ones place, 6 in the tenths place, and 1 in the hundredths place.
Explain why 40.5 and 40.50 have the digit 5 in the same place value.
Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.answer: In both numbers the 5 is in the tenths place — adding a trailing zero after it does not shift any digit’s place value.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: On a number line from 0 to 1 split into tenths, where does 0.3 sit?
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: 0.3 sits three tenth-steps from 0, closer to the 0 end.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: On a number line from 2 to 3 split into tenths, where does 2.7 sit?
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: 2.7 sits seven tenth-steps past 2, closer to the 3 end.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: Which decimal sits exactly halfway between 0 and 1?
Which decimal sits exactly halfway between 4 and 5?
On a hundredths number line between 0.6 and 0.7, where does 0.64 sit?
Order these decimals from LEFT to RIGHT on a number line: 0.8, 0.2, 0.5.
Which is closer to 5 on a number line: 4.6 or 4.9?
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: 4.9 is closer to 5, since it is only 0.1 away.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: Explain step by step how to plot 3.4 on a number line from 3 to 4.
steps: Draw a number line and mark 3 at the left end and 4 at the right end.
Divide the space into 10 equal tenths.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: On a number line from 7 to 8 split into tenths, what decimal is 3 steps past 7?
A runner has completed 0.75 of a 1 km track. Is she closer to the start or the finish?
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: She is closer to the finish (1 km), since 0.75 is only 0.25 away from 1.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: Why does dividing the space between two whole numbers into 10 equal parts represent tenths?
Decimals on the Number Line.answer: A tenth is defined as one of ten equal parts of a whole, so splitting the number line segment into 10 equal parts directly matches the tenths place value.

Decimals on the Number Line.q: On a number line, is 0.45 closer to 0.4 or 0.5?

Converting Fractions ↔ Decimals.q: Convert 0.6 to a fraction in simplest form.
Convert 0.25 to a fraction in simplest form.
Explain step by step how to convert 0.75 to a simplified fraction.
steps: Write the decimal digits as the numerator: 75.
Use 100 as the denominator (2 decimal digits): 75/100.
Find the HCF of 75 and 100, which is 25.

Converting Fractions ↔ Decimals.q: A recipe needs 3/4 cup of sugar. Write this as a decimal.
Why must we simplify a fraction after converting from a decimal?
Converting Fractions ↔ Decimals.answer: Simplifying expresses the fraction in its lowest, cleanest terms by dividing both numerator and denominator by their HCF, making it easier to compare and use.

Converting Fractions ↔ Decimals.q: Convert 0.2 to a fraction in simplest form.
Convert 7/20 to a decimal (Hint: first convert 20 to a denominator of 100).

Word Problems on Decimals.q: Aman buys fruits worth ₹64.50 and vegetables worth ₹28.75. What is the total cost?
Continuing the previous question, if Aman pays with a ₹100 note, how much change does he get?
A rope is 12.5 m long. A piece of 4.75 m is cut off. How much rope is left?
Continuing the previous question, if another 2.5 m piece is cut off, how much rope remains?
A bag of rice weighs 5.6 kg. If 2.35 kg is used, how much remains?
Priya buys a book for ₹85.40 and a pencil box for ₹34.60. What is the total cost?
A jug has 2 litres of juice. 0.75 litres is poured into one glass and 0.5 litres into another. How much juice is left?
A tailor has 6 m of cloth and uses 2.4 m and then 1.85 m for two shirts. How much cloth is left?
A milkman sells 3.5 litres in the morning and 2.75 litres in the evening. How much milk did he sell in total?
A student walks 1.2 km to school and 1.2 km back home, 5 days a week. How far does she walk in one day?
Why is it important to identify keywords like "total" or "remaining" before solving a decimal word problem?
Word Problems on Decimals.answer: These keywords tell you which operation to use — "total" or "altogether" signals addition, while "remaining" or "left" signals subtraction — helping you set up the problem correctly before calculating.

Word Problems on Decimals.q: A shopkeeper had ₹500. He spent ₹123.50 on stock and ₹87.25 on rent. How much money does he have left?

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: Fill in the blank: 3/10 written as a decimal is ______.
Fill in the blank: In 5.62, the digit in the hundredths place is ______.
True or False: 2.3 and 2.30 represent the same value.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: True — a trailing zero does not change a decimal’s value.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: True or False: 0.9 is smaller than 0.19.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: False — 0.9 (9 tenths) is much bigger than 0.19 (1 tenth, 9 hundredths).

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: Fill in the blank: 0.75 simplified as a fraction is ______.
True or False: The hundredths place is the first digit after the decimal point.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: False — the tenths place is first; hundredths is second.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: Fill in the blank: 8 m and 60 cm written as a decimal (in metres) is ______.
True or False: 100 paise written as a decimal of a rupee is 1.00.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: True — 100 paise makes one whole rupee.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: True or False: 4.05 is greater than 4.5.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: False — 4.5 has more tenths (5) than 4.05 (0), so 4.5 is greater.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.q: Fill in the blank: To add decimals, you must first line up the ______.
True or False: 0.06 and 0.6 are the same value.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False Practice.answer: False — 0.06 is six hundredths while 0.6 is six tenths, a much bigger value.

Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Data is a collection of facts, numbers, or observations gathered for a purpose.
To study it, find patterns, and make decisions based on facts instead of guesses.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Is "favourite pet" category data or numerical data?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Category data — pets like Dog, Cat, Fish are groups, not measured numbers.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Is "height of students in cm" category data or numerical data?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Numerical data — height is a measured number.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Give one real-life example of data being collected.
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Any reasonable example, such as recording the daily temperature or the number of students absent each day.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Is "number of rainy days in a month" category or numerical data?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Numerical data — it is a count of days.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Is "favourite ice-cream flavour" category or numerical data?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Category data — flavours are groups, not numbers.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Explain step by step how a class survey on favourite sport becomes usable data.
steps: Ask every student their favourite sport.
Group the answers by sport (Cricket, Football, etc.).
Count how many chose each sport.
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: The recorded, grouped, and counted answers form organized data ready for study.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Why is organizing data more useful than leaving it as a random list?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Organizing data reveals patterns and trends and makes it far easier to read, compare, and use for decisions.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Name two ways data can be collected.
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Observation (watching and recording) and surveys (asking questions).

Introduction to Data Handling.q: Is "number of pets owned" category or numerical data?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Numerical data — it is a measured count.

Introduction to Data Handling.q: A shopkeeper notes down how many customers visit each day. Is this data? Why?
Introduction to Data Handling.answer: Yes — it is a countable fact recorded for a purpose, which is exactly what makes it data.

Recording Data.q: What is the difference between observation and a survey?
Recording Data.answer: Observation means watching and recording facts directly, while a survey means collecting data by asking people questions.

Recording Data.q: What do we call data exactly as it was collected, before organizing?
Arrange this raw data in ascending order: 5, 3, 8, 3.
Arrange this raw data in ascending order: 9, 6, 9, 7.
To find out how many students walk to school, would observation or a survey work better, or both?
Recording Data.answer: Either works — you could observe students arriving, or ask (survey) each student directly.

Recording Data.q: What is the first step before making a tally table or graph?
Recording Data.answer: Collecting and organizing the raw data.

Recording Data.q: Counting birds visiting a garden each morning is an example of which method?
Explain step by step how to organize this raw data into ascending order: 7, 2, 7, 4, 2.
steps: List all the numbers as collected: 7, 2, 7, 4, 2.
Continue picking the next smallest each time.

Recording Data.q: Why might raw data be considered "messy"?
Recording Data.answer: Because it is recorded in the order it was collected, without any grouping or sorting, making patterns hard to see.

Recording Data.q: A teacher asks each student to write down their favourite subject on paper. What data collection method is this?
Arrange this raw data in ascending order: 12, 8, 15, 8, 10.
What is the benefit of organizing raw data into an ordered list?
Recording Data.answer: It makes the data much easier to study, spot patterns in, and later convert into a tally table or graph.

Tally Marks.q: How is the 5th tally mark drawn?
Tally Marks.answer: It is drawn diagonally across the first four vertical lines, forming a bundle of 5.

Tally Marks.q: How many tally lines represent the count 9?
Tally Marks.answer: One bundle of 5 plus 4 single lines = 9 tally lines in total.

Tally Marks.q: If tally marks show 2 full bundles of 5 plus 3 single marks, what is the frequency?
If tally marks show 3 full bundles of 5 plus 1 single mark, what is the frequency?
If tally marks show 4 full bundles of 5 with no extra marks, what is the frequency?
Why are tally marks grouped in bundles of 5?
Tally Marks.answer: Grouping in 5s allows fast counting in multiples of 5 instead of counting one line at a time.

Tally Marks.q: A survey of favourite fruits shows Mango with 2 bundles of 5 and 2 extra marks. How many people chose Mango?
Explain step by step how to draw tally marks for the count 13.
steps: Draw the 5th line diagonally across them to complete a bundle of 5.
Draw another 4 vertical lines for the next bundle.
Draw the 5th diagonal line to complete the second bundle of 5 (total 10).
Draw 3 more single vertical lines for the remaining 3.
Tally Marks.answer: 2 full bundles of 5 plus 3 single lines represents 13.

Tally Marks.q: To count 23 items using tally marks, how many full bundles of 5 and extra marks would you have?
Tally Marks.answer: 23 = (4 × 5) + 3, so 4 full bundles of 5 plus 3 extra single marks.

Tally Marks.q: What is the frequency represented by 1 full bundle of 5 plus 4 single marks?
Why is counting tally marks in bundles faster than counting individual lines?
Tally Marks.answer: Because you can count in steps of 5 (5, 10, 15...) rather than counting one line at a time, which is much quicker for larger numbers.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: What three things does a frequency table typically show for each item?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: The item (or category), its tally marks, and its frequency (final count).

Organizing Data in Tables.q: A table shows Cricket–12, Football–8, Badminton–5. What is the total number of students surveyed?
In the table Cricket–12, Football–8, Badminton–5, which sport is the most popular?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: Cricket, with the highest frequency of 12.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: In the table Cricket–12, Football–8, Badminton–5, which sport is the least popular?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: Badminton, with the lowest frequency of 5.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: A table shows Red–7, Blue–10, Green–4. What is the total surveyed?
A survey of pets shows Dog–6, Cat–9, Fish–3. How many more students have a Cat than a Fish?
A table shows Tea–15, Coffee–9, Juice–6. What is the total number surveyed?
Explain step by step how to build a frequency table from this raw data: A, B, A, C, B, A.
steps: List the unique items: A, B, C.
Write each item with its tally marks and frequency in the table.
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1 in the frequency table.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: Why is a frequency table more useful than a long list of raw data?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: It organizes the raw data into clear categories with counts, so patterns and comparisons become instantly visible.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: To find the total number of items recorded in a frequency table, what should you do?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: Add up every frequency value listed in the table.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: A table shows Maths–18, Science–22, English–14. What subject has the highest frequency, and what is the total?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: Science has the highest frequency (22). Total = 18+22+14 = 54.

Organizing Data in Tables.q: A table shows Summer–9, Winter–14, Rainy–7 (favourite season). What is the total, and which season is least favourite?
Organizing Data in Tables.answer: Total = 9+14+7 = 30. Rainy is the least favourite, with 7 votes.

Pictographs.q: What does a pictograph use to represent data?
Pictographs.answer: Small pictures or symbols, where each symbol represents a fixed number of items shown in the key.

Pictographs.q: What is the purpose of the "key" in a pictograph?
Pictographs.answer: It tells you exactly how many items each picture/symbol represents.

Pictographs.q: If the key says 🍦 = 2 and a row shows 4 pictures, how many ice-creams does that represent?
A pictograph key shows 📕 = 10 books. How many symbols would represent 30 books?
A pictograph key shows ⚽ = 5 students. How many symbols represent 15 students?
What can be used in a pictograph to show a leftover, non-whole amount?
Pictographs.answer: A half-symbol, representing half of the key value.

Pictographs.q: If the key is 🚗 = 4 cars and you need to show 12 cars, how many symbols should you draw?
Explain step by step how to draw a pictograph for this data: Cricket–15, Football–12 (key ⚽ = 5 students).
steps: Football: 12 ÷ 5 = 2 full symbols with 2 leftover, so draw 2 full symbols plus 1 half symbol.
Pictographs.answer: Cricket gets 3 full symbols; Football gets 2 full symbols and 1 half symbol.

Pictographs.q: Why should you choose a key value that divides your data evenly where possible?
Pictographs.answer: It avoids messy half-symbols and keeps the pictograph clean and easy to read.

Pictographs.q: A pictograph key shows 🎈 = 6 balloons. How many symbols would represent 18 balloons?
What is one advantage of a pictograph over a plain frequency table?
Pictographs.answer: A pictograph is more visually engaging and can make comparing categories quicker and more intuitive at a glance.

Pictographs.q: A pictograph key shows 📗 = 4 books. If Class A read 20 books, how many symbols represent Class A?

Interpreting Pictographs.q: To find the value shown by a row in a pictograph, what should you do?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: Count the number of symbols in that row, then multiply by the key value.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: Key: 📗 = 2 books. Kabir’s row shows 5 symbols. How many books did Kabir read?
Key: 📗 = 2 books. Aarav shows 4 symbols and Riya shows 2 symbols. Who read more, and by how many?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: Aarav = 4×2=8 books, Riya = 2×2=4 books. Aarav read 8−4 = 4 more books.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: A pictograph (key 🍎 = 3 apples) shows Monday with 3 symbols and Tuesday with 5 symbols. How many apples were sold on Tuesday?
Continuing the previous question, how many apples were sold in total across both days?
If two rows in a pictograph have the same number of symbols, are their values equal?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: Yes, since both use the same key, equal symbol counts always mean equal values.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: Key: 🎈 = 6 balloons. A row shows 2 full symbols and 1 half symbol. How many balloons in total?
Explain step by step how to compare two rows in a pictograph and find the difference in value.
steps: Count the number of symbols in each row.
Multiply each count by the key value to get actual values.
Subtract the smaller value from the larger value.
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: The result gives exactly how many more/fewer items one row has compared to the other.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: Key: 📕 = 5 books. Class A shows 4 symbols, Class B shows 6 symbols. How many more books did Class B read?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: Class A = 4×5=20, Class B = 6×5=30. Difference = 30−20 = 10 more books.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: Why is it wrong to just count symbols as the final answer in a pictograph question?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: Because each symbol may represent more than 1 item — you must multiply by the key value to get the true total.

Interpreting Pictographs.q: Key: 🚗 = 4 cars. Row A shows 3 symbols, Row B shows 5 symbols. What is the combined total of cars in both rows?
Key: ⚽ = 5 students. If a row shows 1 full symbol and 1 half symbol, how many students does that represent?
Interpreting Pictographs.answer: (1 × 5) + (0.5 × 5) = 5 + 2.5 = 7.5, so about 7 or 8 students depending on rounding.

Bar Graphs.q: What does the height of a bar in a bar graph represent?
Bar Graphs.answer: The frequency or value for that category.

Bar Graphs.q: What is used to measure the exact height of a bar?
Bar Graphs.answer: The numbered scale drawn along the axis.

Bar Graphs.q: If the scale is 1 square = 5 students, how many squares tall should a bar for 20 students be?
If the scale is 1 square = 2 students, how many squares tall should a bar for 12 students be?
A bar graph shows pets owned: Dog reaches 6, Cat reaches 10, Fish reaches 2. Which pet is the most popular?
Bar Graphs.answer: Cat, with the tallest bar reaching 10.

Bar Graphs.q: Why must every bar in a bar graph have the same width?
Bar Graphs.answer: So that only the height shows the difference in values, keeping the comparison between bars fair and accurate.

Bar Graphs.q: If Football = 16 students and the scale is 1 square = 4 students, how many squares tall is the Football bar?
Explain step by step how to draw a bar graph for this data: Cricket–12, Football–8 (scale: 1 square = 2 students).
steps: Draw the axis lines and mark a scale where 1 square = 2 students.
For Cricket (12), draw a bar 12 ÷ 2 = 6 squares tall.
For Football (8), draw a bar 8 ÷ 2 = 4 squares tall.
Keep both bars the same width with an equal gap between them.
Bar Graphs.answer: Cricket bar = 6 squares tall, Football bar = 4 squares tall.

Bar Graphs.q: Why is choosing a sensible scale important when drawing a bar graph?
Bar Graphs.answer: A good scale keeps the graph a manageable size while still clearly showing the differences between bar heights.

Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows Rain (in mm) for 3 months: Jan=20, Feb=35, Mar=15. Using a scale of 1 square = 5mm, how tall is the February bar?
What key feature makes a bar graph easy to compare visually?
Bar Graphs.answer: Bars of equal width with only their height varying, so the eye can instantly judge which category has more or less.

Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows Basketball = 9 students with a scale of 1 square = 3 students. How tall should the bar be?

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: How do you read a bar’s exact value from a bar graph?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: Trace a straight horizontal line from the top of the bar across to the scale on the axis, then read the number.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: If a bar’s top falls exactly between the 10 and 20 marks, what is its approximate value?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: Roughly 15, the halfway point between 10 and 20.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: If the Science bar = 28 and the English bar = 12, what is the difference?
What does the tallest bar in a bar graph always represent?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: The maximum value in the data set.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: What does the shortest bar in a bar graph always represent?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: The minimum value in the data set.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows Maths = 18 and English = 12. How many more students prefer Maths?
A bar graph shows fruit sales: Apple = 25, Mango = 40, Banana = 15. What is the total fruit sold?
Explain step by step how to find the difference between the tallest and shortest bar in a graph.
steps: Identify the tallest bar and read its value from the scale.
Identify the shortest bar and read its value from the scale.
Subtract the shortest bar’s value from the tallest bar’s value.
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: The result gives the difference between the maximum and minimum values.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows Monday = 20 books, Tuesday = 35 books. What is the total for both days?
When subtracting to compare two bars, why must the bigger value come first?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: To avoid getting a negative answer — the larger value minus the smaller value gives a sensible, positive difference.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows temperature (°C) over 3 days: Mon=30, Tue=27, Wed=33. Which day was the hottest, and by how much compared to the coolest day?
Interpreting Bar Graphs.answer: Wednesday was hottest at 33°C. It was 33 − 27 = 6°C warmer than Tuesday, the coolest day.

Interpreting Bar Graphs.q: A bar graph shows votes for class monitor: Aisha = 14, Rohan = 19, Meera = 9. What is the total number of votes cast?

Comparing Data.q: Name the three common ways the same data set can be displayed.
Comparing Data.answer: As a frequency table, a pictograph, or a bar graph.

Comparing Data.q: What is the "maximum" of a data set?
Comparing Data.answer: The highest value in the data set.

Comparing Data.q: What is the "minimum" of a data set?
Comparing Data.answer: The lowest value in the data set.

Comparing Data.q: A table shows Cricket–15, Football–9, Kabaddi–6. What is the total?
In the table Cricket–15, Football–9, Kabaddi–6, what is the maximum?
Comparing Data.answer: Cricket, with the highest value of 15.

Comparing Data.q: A table shows Red–8, Blue–5, Yellow–11. What is the minimum value?
Comparing Data.answer: Blue, with the lowest value of 5.

Comparing Data.q: How do you find the total of a data set shown in a table?
Comparing Data.answer: Add up every value listed in the table.

Comparing Data.q: If a bar graph and a pictograph both display the results of the same class survey, will their values match?
Comparing Data.answer: Yes — since the underlying data is identical, only the visual style differs.

Comparing Data.q: A table shows Red–8, Blue–5, Yellow–11. What is the total?
Explain step by step how to find the maximum, minimum, and total of this data: Apples–14, Oranges–9, Bananas–20.
steps: Identify the highest value as the maximum: 20 (Bananas).
Identify the lowest value as the minimum: 9 (Oranges).
Add all values for the total: 14+9+20 = 43.

Comparing Data.q: Why is it useful to compare data shown in different chart types?
Comparing Data.answer: It helps you choose the clearest way to present or understand the same information, depending on the situation.

Comparing Data.q: A table shows rainfall (mm) over 4 weeks: 12, 25, 8, 19. What is the maximum, minimum, and total rainfall?

Word Problems on Data Handling.q: A tally shows Maths (2 bundles of 5 + 1) and Science (1 bundle of 5 + 2). How many more students chose Maths than Science?
A tally shows Tea (1 bundle of 5 + 3) and Coffee (1 bundle of 5). How many people were surveyed in total?
A bar graph shows books sold: Monday = 20, Tuesday = 35, Wednesday = 15. What is the total for all 3 days?
Continuing the previous question, how many more books were sold on Tuesday than Wednesday?
A pictograph (key 🚗 = 4 cars) shows Red = 3 symbols, Blue = 2 symbols. How many more red cars are there than blue cars?
A survey shows tally marks for pets: Dog (1 bundle of 5 + 2), Cat (2 bundles of 5). How many students have a Cat?
A pictograph (key 📗 = 5 books) shows Class A = 4 symbols and Class B = 3 symbols. How many books did both classes read together?
Word Problems on Data Handling.answer: Class A = 4×5=20, Class B = 3×5=15. Total = 20+15 = 35 books.

Word Problems on Data Handling.q: Explain step by step how to solve this word problem: A bar graph shows Rainy days: June=8, July=15, August=10. Which month had the most rainy days, and how many more than June?
steps: Compare the values: June=8, July=15, August=10.
Word Problems on Data Handling.answer: July had the most rainy days (15), which is 7 more than June.

Word Problems on Data Handling.q: A bar graph shows fruit sales: Apple = 25, Mango = 40, Banana = 15. What is the total fruit sold?
A pictograph (key 🎈 = 6 balloons) shows Party A = 3 symbols and Party B = 2 symbols. How many more balloons did Party A have?
Word Problems on Data Handling.answer: Party A = 3×6=18, Party B = 2×6=12. Difference = 18−12 = 6 more balloons.

Word Problems on Data Handling.q: A tally for favourite colours shows Red (2 bundles of 5), Blue (1 bundle of 5 + 4), Green (1 bundle of 5 + 1). What is the total number of students surveyed?
A bar graph shows votes: Aisha=14, Rohan=19, Meera=9. Who won, and by how many votes over the second-highest?
Word Problems on Data Handling.answer: Rohan won with 19 votes, which is 19 − 14 = 5 more votes than Aisha, the second-highest.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False.q: Fill in the blank: a collection of facts and figures gathered for a purpose is called ______.
Fill in the blank: the 5th tally mark is drawn ______ across the first four.
True or False: raw data is already sorted into a neat table.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False.answer: False — raw data is unsorted, exactly as originally collected.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False.q: Fill in the blank: in a pictograph, the box that tells you what each symbol is worth is called the ______.
True or False: in a bar graph, the height of a bar shows its value.
Fill in the Blanks & True/False.answer: True — the height directly represents the value.

Fill in the Blanks & True/False.q: Fill in the blank: the highest value in a data set is called the ______.
